item.content:encoded:
Starting a career after university can be challenging, particularly for graduates who are looking for an opportunity that combines professional training, practical experience, mentorship, and exposure to a global business environment. PwC offers a range of student and graduate opportunities designed to help university students and recent graduates transition into professional careers while developing the technical, business, leadership, and interpersonal skills required in today’s workplace.

The PwC student and graduate opportunities include several pathways for different stages of academic and professional development. These include graduate opportunities for recent university graduates, the China Sourcing Initiative for eligible students studying in the United States and Canada, the Deals—Edge graduate programme, the Assurance Remote Team Member programme, the Hong Kong Assurance Apprenticeship Programme, internships, and the LEAP programme.

These opportunities can be particularly valuable for students and graduates interested in professional services, accounting, auditing, business advisory, deals, and other corporate career pathways. Depending on the programme, applicants may receive structured training, career coaching, work-buddy support, practical project experience, exposure to experienced professionals, professional development opportunities, and potential pathways into longer-term employment.

The programmes have different eligibility requirements, academic levels, locations, and starting periods. Therefore, prospective applicants should carefully review the requirements for the specific programme they intend to pursue before submitting an application.

PwC Student and Graduate Opportunities at a Glance

PwC’s student and graduate opportunities are divided broadly into opportunities for graduates and opportunities for undergraduate or current university students.

Graduate Opportunities

The graduate-level opportunities featured include:

  • General Graduate Programme
  • China Sourcing Initiative
  • Deals—Edge
  • Assurance Remote Team Member (RTM)

Undergraduate and Student Opportunities

The student-focused opportunities include:

  • Apprenticeship
  • Internship
  • LEAP

This structure allows students to identify an opportunity according to their current stage of education, expected graduation year, academic background, and career interests.

1. PwC General Graduate Opportunities

The PwC General Graduate Programme is designed for recent graduates who are ready to begin their professional careers and develop into trusted business advisers.

PwC describes the programme as an opportunity for individuals who are passionate about teamwork, making a difference, and working in a firm that provides opportunities across a broad range of industries.

One of the major advantages of the graduate programme is its focus on structured professional development. Successful applicants receive training connected to the service area to which they are allocated.

The programme also provides support from experienced professionals, including a career coach and work buddy. This can help graduates understand their responsibilities, adapt to the professional environment, and develop their careers from the beginning.

According to the opportunity information, PwC welcomes applications from graduates of 2025, 2026, and 2027 who hold a bachelor’s degree or above. All majors are eligible.

What Does the PwC Graduate Programme Offer?

The programme is structured to help graduates make a successful transition from university into professional employment.

Key features include:

  • Entry-level professional training.
  • Training related to the applicant’s allocated service area.
  • Support from an experienced career coach.
  • Guidance from a work buddy.
  • Exposure to a broad range of industries.
  • Opportunities to work collaboratively as part of a professional team.
  • Development of skills needed to become a trusted business adviser.

For graduates who have limited professional experience, the combination of structured training, coaching, and practical workplace exposure can provide an important foundation for their careers.

PwC General Graduate Application Process

The application journey consists of several stages:

  1. Online application
  2. Online assessment
  3. Meeting with PwC
  4. PwC Superday
  5. Receiving an offer
  6. Offer celebration

The first step is the online application. Applicants are required to provide basic personal information as well as academic achievements and professional background information relevant to the job requirements.

When Does the General Graduate Programme Start?

The information provided states that the programme starts from August 2026.

General Graduate Eligibility

Applicants should have:

  • Graduated in 2025, 2026, or 2027.
  • A bachelor’s degree or above.
  • Any academic major, as all majors are eligible.

The source does not specify a particular nationality, race, or African-country eligibility requirement for the General Graduate Programme. Therefore, applicants should consult the specific vacancy and application conditions for the relevant PwC location.

2. PwC China Sourcing Initiative

The China Sourcing Initiative, commonly referred to as CSI, is a graduate programme designed for overseas students who want to begin their professional careers with PwC in Chinese Mainland, Hong Kong SAR, or Macau SAR.

The initiative specifically targets students in the United States and Canada who aspire to join PwC in full-time Associate positions.

An important feature of the programme is its remote application process. Eligible candidates do not need to travel back to Chinese Mainland, Hong Kong SAR, or Macau SAR during the application process because PwC facilitates the application through online assessments and virtual interviews.

Who Can Apply for the China Sourcing Initiative?

According to the provided information, applicants must:

  • Be studying at a university in the United States or Canada.
  • Hold a bachelor’s degree or above, or be pursuing such a degree.
  • Graduate between August 2025 and August 2027.
  • Meet the relevant work eligibility requirements.
  • Be eligible to work in Chinese Mainland and Macau SAR without a working visa.

For selected Associates working in Hong Kong SAR, PwC will provide Hong Kong SAR working visa sponsorship.

CSI Application Process

The China Sourcing Initiative application journey includes:

  1. Online application.
  2. Online assessment.
  3. Information session.
  4. Virtual interviews.
  5. Receiving an offer.
  6. Starting with PwC.

Applicants provide personal details together with their academic and professional background as part of the application process.

CSI Starting Period

The source states that the opportunity starts from August 2026.

3. PwC Deals—Edge Graduate Programme

The Deals—Edge programme is a graduate opportunity within PwC Deals EMEA and Asia Pacific.

It is designed to attract, develop, and retain talented graduates and help them build early-career skills in the Deals business.

The programme is particularly relevant to graduates who are interested in developing careers as Deals advisers and working in an international professional-services environment.

PwC describes Edge as a programme intended to launch graduate careers in an international Deals environment. It combines professional development with practical exposure and opportunities to work across different areas of the Deals business.

What Does the Deals—Edge Programme Include?

The programme features a combination of:

  • International development opportunities.
  • Rotations across different Deals business units.
  • Potential international rotations.
  • Regular professional learning.
  • Technical learning.
  • Opportunities to complete a professional qualification.
  • Development of early-career Deals skills.
  • Exposure to an international Deals environment.

Some rotations may be international, giving participants the possibility of gaining experience across different markets and business environments.

The programme is intended to help participants develop into the next generation of highly valued Deals advisers who can deliver sustainable outcomes and build trust with clients.

Who Is Eligible for PwC Edge?

PwC welcomes applications from:

  • 2025 graduates.
  • 2026 graduates.
  • 2027 graduates.
  • Applicants with a bachelor’s degree or above.
  • Applicants from all academic majors.

The source explicitly states that there are no restrictions based on academic major for the listed graduate eligibility.

Deals—Edge Application Process

The application journey includes:

  1. Online application.
  2. Online assessment.
  3. Meeting with PwC.
  4. PwC Superday.
  5. Receiving an offer.
  6. Offer celebration.

The programme states that applications start from August 2026.

4. PwC Assurance Remote Team Member Programme

The Assurance Remote Team Member, or RTM, programme reflects PwC’s efforts to integrate technology and remote working into the audit and assurance environment.

The programme was established through Remote Team Member Centres in Wuhan and Chengdu to provide high-quality audit services to clients while working remotely with engagement teams.

The RTM model combines traditional audit experience with information technology, standardized processes, flexible resource scheduling, and digital applications.

This approach is designed to improve audit efficiency, process quality, and delivery capacity while supporting PwC’s broader digital transformation.

Key Features of the PwC RTM Programme

1. Flexibility

The remote working model is designed to reduce unnecessary business travel and inefficient overtime.

It also aims to improve audit quality and delivery through flexible resource planning while helping employees achieve a better work-life balance.

2. Team Stability

The RTM model maintains a permanent team of partners.

This allows employees to benefit from ongoing coaching, stronger professional relationships, and greater efficiency through consistent teamwork.

3. Standardisation

The programme integrates audit processes and procedures using a relatively standardized approach.

Standardization is intended to improve audit quality while maintaining the integrity and consistency of audit processes.

4. Digitalisation

Technology plays an important role in RTM.

Participants work with PwC’s digital tools as part of the audit process. These tools are intended to improve audit efficiency and contribute to the transformation of traditional auditing into more technology-enabled and intelligent audit practices.

5. Professional Growth

RTM also provides opportunities for learning and career development.

Senior Associates can take on responsibilities that involve managing and coaching team members, allowing them to strengthen project management and multitasking skills.

Associates are organized by industry, which can give them broader exposure to industry-specific accounting knowledge and practical experience.

6. Diversity of Services

The RTM initiative also aims to expand beyond traditional audit services by drawing on audit experience and industry knowledge to develop more diversified services based on industry research and insights.

RTM Application Process

The listed application journey includes:

  1. Online application.
  2. Online assessment.
  3. Meeting with PwC.
  4. PwC Superday.
  5. Receiving an offer.
  6. Offer celebration.

The opportunity information states that applications start from August 2026.

The supplied source does not provide a separate detailed eligibility list for the RTM opportunity, such as nationality, degree requirements, or graduation year. Applicants should therefore check the specific RTM vacancy when applying.

5. PwC Hong Kong Assurance Apprenticeship Programme

The PwC Hong Kong Assurance Apprenticeship Programme is designed for undergraduate students who want to gain professional experience while completing their university education.

The programme is described as a fast-track opportunity for students interested in building careers in the accounting profession.

Participants receive both formal and on-the-job training similar to PwC graduate recruits. They can also gain exposure to a broad range of projects and work with experienced managers involved in professional development and talent development.

Who Can Apply?

The programme is open to:

  • Year 2 undergraduate students.
  • Students studying accounting.

Participants are expected to complete two full terms of employment:

  • January–May 2027.
  • January–May 2028.

These employment periods take place while participants continue completing their four-year undergraduate degrees.

Successful apprentices who meet the required performance standard can have their careers fast-tracked by returning as Year 2 Associates after graduation.

Apprenticeship Application Process

The application process includes:

  1. Online application.
  2. Online assessment.
  3. Meeting with PwC.
  4. Interview.
  5. Receiving an offer.
  6. Starting with PwC.

The application form asks candidates to provide personal information and academic and professional background details.

6. PwC Internship Programme

PwC also offers internships for students who want to gain professional experience before graduating.

The internship programme provides an opportunity to work alongside experienced professionals, experience PwC’s organizational culture, explore career interests, and prepare for future professional employment.

The source states that PwC has two internship intakes per year: Summer and Winter, with opportunities available across different lines of service.

What Can Students Gain From a PwC Internship?

The internship can provide students with:

  • Practical workplace experience.
  • Exposure to experienced professionals.
  • An opportunity to understand PwC’s working culture.
  • Exposure to different lines of service.
  • An opportunity to explore career aspirations.
  • Preparation for future professional employment.
  • Potential progression into the graduate recruitment process.

Importantly, the source states that strong-performing interns may have the opportunity to be fast-tracked through the graduate recruitment process.

Who Is Eligible for the PwC Internship?

The provided information states that PwC welcomes applications from graduates of 2028 and beyond with a bachelor’s degree or above, and all majors are eligible.

Internship Starting Period

The source states that the internship starts from Autumn 2026.

PwC Internship Application Process

The listed process includes:

  1. Online application.
  2. Online assessment.
  3. Interview.
  4. Receiving an offer.
  5. Starting with PwC.

Applicants are asked to provide their personal information as well as academic and professional background details.

7. PwC LEAP Programme

The LEAP programme is another early-career opportunity focused on developing future talent.

Rather than being limited to technical professional training, LEAP places emphasis on creativity, relationships, problem-solving, insight, agility, and leadership.

Participants, known as LEAPers, are invited to take part in leadership and business training events and may also have the opportunity to contribute to campus recruitment activities and initiatives that promote the PwC brand.

What Skills Does PwC LEAP Focus On?

The programme highlights several capabilities that are increasingly important in modern professional environments:

  • Creativity.
  • Relationship building.
  • Problem-solving.
  • Insight.
  • Agility.
  • Leadership.

The programme is designed around the idea that professional success requires more than technical knowledge. It also requires the ability to collaborate, adapt, influence, solve problems, and contribute to organizational initiatives.

Benefits of Becoming a PwC LEAPer

According to the opportunity information, LEAP participants can:

Learn

Participants learn about PwC while connecting their curiosity and interests with opportunities to contribute to society.

Explore

They can experience a diverse and inclusive culture that emphasizes people and provides opportunities for growth and development.

Advance

Participants can develop skills intended to prepare them for the future workplace.

Experience PwC

The programme provides an opportunity to experience an environment where people and technology work together to accomplish more.

Who Is Eligible for PwC LEAP?

The eligibility requirements differ according to location.

Chinese Mainland or Macau SAR

Eligible students include:

  • First-year bachelor students.
  • Second-year bachelor students.
  • First-year master students.

Hong Kong SAR or Overseas

Eligible students include:

  • First-year bachelor students.
  • Second-year bachelor students.

The source also states that all schools and majors are welcome.

LEAP Application Process

The listed application journey includes:

  1. Online application.
  2. Online assessment.
  3. LEAP Day.
  4. Receiving an offer.

The source lists the LEAP period as February–March 2026 and asks applicants to provide information concerning their personal details, leadership experience, personal influence, and campus relationships.

Because the supplied information lists February–March 2026 for LEAP, prospective applicants should verify the current application cycle and dates directly on PwC’s official careers page before applying.

How to Choose the Right PwC Opportunity

With several programmes available, students and graduates should select an opportunity based on their current academic status and career objectives.

If You Graduated in 2025, 2026, or 2027

The General Graduate Programme may be relevant because PwC specifically welcomes graduates from these years and accepts applicants with bachelor’s degrees or above from all majors.

The Deals—Edge programme is another option for graduates interested in developing a career in Deals and professional advisory services.

If You Are Studying in the United States or Canada

The China Sourcing Initiative may be particularly relevant if you expect to graduate between August 2025 and August 2027 and meet the programme’s work-eligibility requirements.

If You Are a Year 2 Accounting Student

The Hong Kong Assurance Apprenticeship Programme is specifically designed for Year 2 undergraduate students studying accounting.

If You Expect to Graduate in 2028 or Later

The PwC Internship Programme may be a suitable pathway for gaining practical experience before graduation.

If You Are an Early-Year University Student

The LEAP programme is designed for eligible first- and second-year bachelor’s students and, in the Chinese Mainland and Macau SAR, first-year master’s students.

Why PwC Student and Graduate Opportunities Are Valuable

Early-career opportunities can provide more than a first job. They can help students and graduates build the professional foundation necessary for long-term career development.

PwC’s programmes combine several elements that can be particularly valuable at the beginning of a career.

Structured Training

Several programmes provide formal or role-specific training, allowing participants to develop professional knowledge in a structured environment.

Practical Experience

Internships, apprenticeships, graduate programmes, and RTM opportunities allow participants to gain exposure to real professional work rather than relying exclusively on classroom learning.

Mentorship and Coaching

The General Graduate Programme specifically mentions career coaches and work buddies, providing new graduates with additional guidance as they enter professional employment.

International Exposure

Some programmes, particularly Deals—Edge and the China Sourcing Initiative, are structured around international or cross-border career opportunities.

Professional Qualifications

Deals—Edge includes the opportunity to complete a professional qualification, which can support participants pursuing long-term professional-services careers.

Leadership Development

LEAP emphasizes leadership, creativity, relationships, agility, and problem-solving, making it particularly relevant for students interested in developing broader workplace capabilities.

Potential Career Progression

Some programmes provide potential pathways into longer-term employment. For example, strong internship performance may lead to fast-tracking in the graduate recruitment process, while successful Apprenticeship participants may return as Year 2 Associates after graduation.

Important Application Information

Applicants should understand that the programmes do not all have identical requirements.

Before applying, candidates should carefully review:

  • The specific programme they are applying for.
  • Graduation-year requirements.
  • Degree requirements.
  • Academic major requirements.
  • Location requirements.
  • Work authorization requirements.
  • Application and assessment stages.
  • Interview requirements.
  • Programme start dates.

For example, the General Graduate and Deals—Edge programmes accept graduates from several graduation years and all majors, while the Hong Kong Assurance Apprenticeship Programme specifically targets Year 2 accounting students. The China Sourcing Initiative has specific requirements concerning where candidates study and their eligibility to work in the relevant locations.

Is There an Application Deadline?

The supplied opportunity information does not provide a single application deadline for the PwC student and graduate opportunities as a whole.

Instead, it provides programme-specific application periods and starting periods, including:

  • General Graduate Programme: starts from August 2026.
  • China Sourcing Initiative: starts from August 2026.
  • Deals—Edge: starts from August 2026.
  • Assurance RTM: starts from August 2026.
  • PwC Internship: starts from Autumn 2026.
  • LEAP: February–March 2026 as listed in the supplied source.

Applicants should therefore check the relevant programme’s application page for the current deadline and availability before submitting an application.

Who Should Consider Applying?

These opportunities may be suitable for:

  • Recent university graduates.
  • Students approaching graduation.
  • Undergraduate students seeking professional experience.
  • Accounting students interested in assurance careers.
  • Students interested in professional services.
  • Graduates interested in Deals and advisory careers.
  • Students seeking internships.
  • Students interested in leadership development.
  • Candidates interested in international career opportunities.
  • Students and graduates seeking structured professional training.

However, eligibility differs significantly between programmes, so applicants should not assume that meeting the requirements of one PwC opportunity automatically makes them eligible for all other programmes.

Application Tips for PwC Student and Graduate Opportunities

1. Select the Correct Programme

Do not apply randomly across programmes. Start by identifying whether you are a graduate, undergraduate student, accounting student, or student studying overseas.

2. Check Your Graduation Year

Graduation year is an important eligibility factor for several programmes.

For example, General Graduate and Deals—Edge specifically identify 2025, 2026, and 2027 graduates, while the internship opportunity identifies graduates of 2028 and beyond.

3. Prepare Your Academic Information

Applicants should have accurate information about their academic achievements and degree history because the application process asks for academic background.

4. Prepare Your Professional Background

Even where extensive professional experience is not required, applicants should prepare information about internships, projects, leadership activities, volunteering, extracurricular activities, and other experiences that demonstrate relevant capabilities.

5. Prepare for Online Assessments

Several of the programmes include an online assessment. Candidates should therefore be prepared to complete assessment stages after submitting their applications.

6. Prepare for Interviews

Some pathways include meetings with PwC, interviews, virtual interviews, or PwC Superday activities. Applicants should be prepared to explain their motivation, academic background, skills, career interests, and reasons for wanting to join PwC.

7. Highlight Transferable Skills

Students and graduates should demonstrate skills such as:

  • Communication.
  • Teamwork.
  • Problem-solving.
  • Leadership.
  • Adaptability.
  • Analytical thinking.
  • Relationship building.
  • Digital skills.
  • Professional curiosity.

These capabilities are particularly relevant because the different programmes emphasize collaboration, leadership, problem-solving, technical development, and professional growth.

PwC Student and Graduate Opportunities 2026: Key Takeaways

PwC provides multiple pathways for students and recent graduates rather than offering a single early-career programme.

The General Graduate Programme is designed for recent graduates and provides structured training, career coaching, and work-buddy support.

The China Sourcing Initiative provides a route for eligible students in the United States and Canada seeking Associate opportunities in Chinese Mainland, Hong Kong SAR, or Macau SAR.

The Deals—Edge programme focuses on developing graduates into future Deals advisers through international development opportunities, rotations, technical learning, professional learning, and potential professional qualifications.

The Assurance Remote Team Member programme combines audit expertise with remote working, standardized processes, digital tools, and professional development.

The Hong Kong Assurance Apprenticeship Programme provides Year 2 accounting students with an opportunity to gain substantial work experience while completing their degrees.

The PwC Internship Programme enables students to gain workplace exposure before graduation and may provide a pathway toward graduate recruitment for strong performers.

The LEAP programme focuses on future talent development through leadership, creativity, relationships, problem-solving, agility, and business training.

Conclusion

PwC’s student and graduate opportunities provide multiple entry points into professional careers for university students and recent graduates at different stages of their education.

Rather than relying solely on academic qualifications, the programmes provide opportunities to develop practical workplace experience, technical knowledge, leadership capabilities, professional relationships, and industry exposure. Depending on the programme, participants may also receive coaching, structured training, international development opportunities, professional learning, and potential pathways toward longer-term employment.

For graduates, the General Graduate and Deals—Edge programmes provide opportunities to begin professional careers and develop specialized expertise. For eligible students studying in the United States and Canada, the China Sourcing Initiative provides an international pathway into PwC’s operations in Chinese Mainland, Hong Kong SAR, and Macau SAR. Accounting students can explore the Hong Kong Assurance Apprenticeship Programme, while students graduating in 2028 and beyond may consider the internship pathway. Early-year students may also find the LEAP programme relevant to their stage of study.

Because eligibility, location, graduation-year requirements, and application dates vary considerably between programmes, prospective applicants should identify the programme that matches their circumstances and carefully review the official application requirements before applying.

The supplied opportunity information does not state one universal application deadline for all PwC student and graduate programmes. Instead, it provides different programme starting periods, so applicants should verify the current application status and deadline for their chosen programme before submitting an application.

item.content:encoded:
The 2026 Africa Intellectual Property Day (#2026AIPD) is highlighting the growing importance of intellectual property in strengthening African businesses, innovation, trade and economic development under the African Continental Free Trade Area (AfCFTA).

Under the theme “Growing Business Under The AfCFTA IP Ecosystem,” the initiative seeks to recognize exceptional accomplishments involving intellectual property, particularly achievements that contribute to the implementation and operationalisation of the AfCFTA Protocol on Intellectual Property Rights.

A central component of the 2026 Africa Intellectual Property Day initiative is the SG Prize, which recognizes an outstanding individual or entity whose work demonstrates meaningful use or generation of an intellectual property right, process or mechanism in the context of the AfCFTA.

The recognition is intended to celebrate African innovators, creators, entrepreneurs, institutions and other stakeholders whose intellectual property-related work produces tangible economic, social or cultural value and has the potential to inspire similar achievements across the continent.

2026 Africa Intellectual Property Day

Africa’s expanding continental market presents significant opportunities for businesses, innovators, creators and institutions. However, intellectual property protection and effective use are important components of ensuring that African innovation can generate sustainable value within this market.

The 2026 Africa Intellectual Property Day focuses attention on the relationship between intellectual property and the implementation of the AfCFTA. Its theme, “Growing Business Under The AfCFTA IP Ecosystem,” reflects the role intellectual property can play in helping African enterprises develop, protect and commercialize their ideas, brands, inventions, creative works and other forms of intellectual assets.

The initiative also provides an opportunity to showcase accomplishments that demonstrate how intellectual property can contribute to:

  • Business growth and competitiveness
  • Cross-border trade within Africa
  • Innovation and technology development
  • Employment creation
  • Export growth
  • Community development
  • Cultural preservation
  • Recognition of African creativity and invention
  • Greater use of intellectual property systems across African markets

What Is the SG Prize?

The SG Prize is a recognition for an exceptional accomplishment by an individual or entity in any domain involving technology, cooperation, economy, trade, law or business where the achievement involves or targets the use or generation of an intellectual property right, process or mechanism in the context of the AfCFTA.

The prize is designed to celebrate individuals and organisations contributing to the development and operationalisation of the AfCFTA IP Ecosystem.

Rather than simply recognizing an idea or an untested concept, the SG Prize places emphasis on verifiable intellectual property use and demonstrable impact.

This means that nominees should be able to show evidence that their intellectual property has been formally registered and applied and that it has generated a concrete outcome.

What Types of Intellectual Property Can Be Considered?

The SG Prize guidelines identify several forms of intellectual property that may qualify, including:

  • Copyright – protection associated with literary, artistic, creative and other eligible original works.
  • Trademarks – intellectual property associated with brands, names, symbols, signs and other identifiers.
  • Patents – protection associated with qualifying inventions and technological innovations.
  • Geographical Indications (GIs) – intellectual property connected to products whose characteristics, reputation or qualities are linked to a particular geographical origin.
  • Plant Variety Rights – intellectual property protection associated with qualifying new plant varieties.

Applicants and nominees should therefore identify the relevant intellectual property right associated with the achievement and provide appropriate evidence demonstrating that it has been formally registered and used.

Key Eligibility and Evaluation Criteria for the SG Prize

The SG Prize guidelines establish several important criteria that submissions should satisfy.

1. Verifiable Intellectual Property Use

The first requirement is that the nominee must have formally registered and applied intellectual property.

The relevant IP may involve:

  • Copyright
  • Trademark
  • Patent
  • Geographical indication
  • Plant variety right

Importantly, the guidelines require evidence supporting the intellectual property claim. Such evidence should either be publicly available or submitted alongside the nomination.

This requirement means that applicants should avoid relying solely on general descriptions of an invention, business, creative project or innovation. The submission should demonstrate that the intellectual property exists within an identifiable and verifiable protection or registration framework and that it has actually been applied.

2. Demonstrable Impact

The intellectual property must have produced a concrete outcome.

The guidelines recognize three broad forms of impact:

Economic impact

Examples may include:

  • Increased income
  • Export growth
  • Business expansion
  • Job creation
  • Commercialisation of an innovation
  • Increased market access
  • Improved business competitiveness

Social impact

Examples may include:

  • Community benefits
  • Increased public access
  • Improved services
  • Support for communities
  • Wider access to useful products or innovations

Cultural impact

Examples may include:

  • Preservation of cultural heritage
  • Protection or promotion of cultural expressions
  • Recognition of artistic achievements
  • Strengthening of African cultural identity

The application should therefore move beyond simply stating that an innovation has been successful. The impact statement should explain what changed as a result of the intellectual property and provide evidence supporting that change.

The guidelines specifically indicate that vague claims are insufficient.

3. African Origin and Reach

Another important criterion is the African origin of the work, innovation or creation.

The work must originate in an African Union (AU) Member State.

The guidelines also indicate that achievements demonstrating cross-border or AfCFTA-relevant impact score more highly.

This makes the relationship between the intellectual property achievement and the broader African market particularly important.

For example, a submission can be strengthened if it demonstrates how an intellectual property asset:

  • Expanded beyond its original national market
  • Supports African cross-border commerce
  • Facilitates trade between African countries
  • Creates opportunities under the AfCFTA
  • Demonstrates potential for wider continental adoption

4. Role-Model Potential

The SG Prize also considers whether the innovation or achievement can serve as an example for other Africans.

The guidelines emphasize that the innovation should be transferable and inspiring.

This means that a strong submission should demonstrate not only what the nominee achieved but also why the achievement matters to other entrepreneurs, innovators, creators, businesses or institutions across Africa.

A successful nominee should ideally demonstrate that their experience can provide a model that others can learn from, adapt or build upon.

5. Consent and Verifiability

Nominees must consent to being:

  • Publicly named
  • Quoted
  • Featured

In addition, all claims associated with the nomination must be verifiable through either:

  • Publicly available information, or
  • Supporting documents submitted with the nomination

Applicants should therefore ensure that information included in the submission is accurate and supported by appropriate documentation.

Who Can Be Nominated for the SG Prize?

The submission form provides two types of submission:

  1. Individual
  2. Institution

The recognition therefore accommodates both individual accomplishments and institutional achievements.

The opportunity is particularly relevant to individuals or entities that have developed, registered and applied intellectual property in an African context and can demonstrate measurable economic, social or cultural impact.

Potentially relevant nominees may include innovators, entrepreneurs, creators, technology developers, businesses, institutions and other organisations whose intellectual property-related accomplishments satisfy the stated criteria.

What Should the 200-Word Impact Statement Include?

One of the most important parts of the submission is the 200-word impact statement.

The form specifically asks applicants to provide a 200-word impact statement based on the SG Prize criteria.

A strong statement should therefore focus on evidence rather than general descriptions.

Applicants should consider addressing the following questions:

What intellectual property was developed or used?

Clearly identify the relevant IP right, process or mechanism.

For example, explain whether the achievement involves a patent, trademark, copyright, geographical indication or plant variety right.

Has the intellectual property been formally registered?

Explain where and how the IP has been registered, where relevant, and provide supporting evidence.

How has the intellectual property been applied?

Describe how the intellectual property is being used in practice rather than simply describing the idea behind it.

What measurable impact has it created?

Explain the concrete results generated by the IP.

Depending on the achievement, this could include:

  • Income generated
  • Jobs created
  • Export opportunities
  • Business growth
  • Community benefits
  • Public access
  • Cultural preservation
  • Artistic recognition

How is the achievement relevant to Africa and the AfCFTA?

Applicants should explain the African dimension of the achievement and, where applicable, demonstrate cross-border or AfCFTA-related relevance.

Why can the achievement inspire others?

Explain what makes the innovation transferable, scalable, replicable or inspirational for other Africans.

Supporting Documents and Evidence

Applicants are required to upload relevant supporting evidence.

The submission system allows supporting evidence to be provided in either of two formats:

  • One ZIP folder, or
  • Up to 10 separate PDF files

The maximum total file size for the uploaded evidence is 100MB.

Applicants should organize their supporting documentation carefully so that the evidence directly supports the claims made in the nomination.

Possible supporting documentation may include relevant official registration evidence, documentation demonstrating application or use of the intellectual property, evidence of impact, publicly verifiable records and other materials that substantiate the submission.

The strongest supporting evidence should directly connect the intellectual property to the claimed economic, social or cultural outcomes.

Information Required in the Application Form

The submission form requires applicants to provide several key details.

These include:

  1. Email address
  2. Full name of the applicant
  3. Type of submission
    • Individual
    • Institution
  4. Country of origin of the applicant
  5. 200-word description of impact
  6. Relevant supporting evidence

Applicants should ensure that all information entered in the form is accurate and consistent with the supporting documentation.

SG Prize Submission Deadline

The deadline for submitting nominations for the SG Prize is: 31 August 2026

Applicants should not wait until the final day to prepare their submissions, particularly where supporting documents need to be collected, converted into PDF files or compressed into a ZIP folder.

Early preparation can also provide an opportunity to review the 200-word impact statement and ensure that it addresses the eligibility and evaluation criteria.

How to Prepare a Strong SG Prize Submission

Applicants can improve the quality of their submission by taking a structured approach.

Step 1: Identify the Intellectual Property

Begin by clearly identifying the intellectual property associated with the achievement.

Determine whether the relevant asset involves a:

  • Patent
  • Trademark
  • Copyright
  • Geographical indication
  • Plant variety right

Step 2: Gather Verification

Collect documentation demonstrating that the intellectual property has been formally registered and applied.

The evidence should be clear enough to allow the claim to be verified.

Step 3: Quantify the Impact

Where possible, use specific evidence to demonstrate results.

For example, instead of simply stating that an innovation created economic benefits, explain the measurable outcome, such as increased income, additional employment, export activity or expansion into new markets.

Similarly, social and cultural impact should be explained through concrete results rather than broad statements.

Step 4: Establish the African Connection

Explain where the innovation or creation originated and how it relates to an AU Member State.

If the achievement has reached multiple African markets or has a clear relationship with AfCFTA implementation, make this connection explicit.

Step 5: Demonstrate Role-Model Potential

Explain why other African innovators, businesses, institutions or creators could learn from or adapt the achievement.

This is particularly important because the SG Prize seeks to recognize achievements that are transferable and inspiring.

Step 6: Prepare the 200-Word Statement

The impact statement should be concise but evidence-driven.

Because the form specifically limits the impact statement to 200 words, applicants should prioritize:

  • The intellectual property
  • Verification
  • Application
  • Measurable impact
  • African origin and reach
  • AfCFTA relevance
  • Role-model potential

Step 7: Organize the Supporting Evidence

Ensure that all supporting documents are readable and relevant.

Applicants can submit either one ZIP folder or up to 10 PDF files, with a maximum combined file size of 100MB.

Why Intellectual Property Matters Under the AfCFTA

The AfCFTA is intended to strengthen economic integration and create greater opportunities for trade across African markets. Intellectual property is an important part of this ecosystem because businesses and innovators depend on intellectual assets to distinguish products, protect inventions, develop brands, preserve creative works and commercialize innovations.

For African businesses seeking to expand beyond their domestic markets, intellectual property can provide an important foundation for protecting and developing their competitive advantages.

The 2026 Africa Intellectual Property Day theme therefore draws attention to the connection between intellectual property, business growth and continental trade integration.

Recognizing successful examples can help demonstrate how intellectual property can be transformed from a legal concept into a practical tool for economic, social and cultural development.

APPLY HERE

Key Details at a Glance

  • Opportunity: 2026 Africa Intellectual Property Day – SG Prize
  • Theme: “Growing Business Under The AfCFTA IP Ecosystem”
  • Recognition: SG Prize
  • Submission types: Individual or Institution
  • Focus: Intellectual property use or generation in the context of the AfCFTA
  • Eligible IP areas: Copyright, trademarks, patents, geographical indications and plant variety rights
  • Impact areas: Economic, social and cultural
  • Geographical requirement: Work, innovation or creation must originate in an AU Member State
  • Supporting evidence: One ZIP folder or up to 10 PDF files
  • Maximum evidence size: 100MB total
  • Impact statement: 200 words
  • Deadline: 31 August 2026

Conclusion

The 2026 Africa Intellectual Property Day SG Prize provides an opportunity to recognize exceptional intellectual property achievements that contribute to Africa’s economic, social and cultural development under the AfCFTA framework.

The initiative goes beyond recognizing ideas alone. The SG Prize emphasizes formally registered and applied intellectual property, verifiable evidence, measurable impact, African origin, AfCFTA relevance and the ability to inspire other Africans.

Individuals and institutions with qualifying achievements should carefully document their intellectual property, demonstrate the concrete results it has produced and clearly explain its relevance to the wider African market.

With the submission deadline set for 31 August 2026, eligible applicants and nominees should begin preparing their 200-word impact statement and supporting evidence as early as possible. A well-organized submission that directly addresses each SG Prize criterion can effectively communicate the significance and wider potential of an intellectual property achievement.

The 2026 Africa Intellectual Property Day theme ultimately highlights an important message for African innovators and businesses: intellectual property can be more than protection for an idea or creation; when effectively developed and applied, it can become a tool for business growth, innovation, employment, trade, cultural preservation and stronger participation in Africa’s emerging continental market.

item.content:encoded:
The UK–Nigeria Season of Culture 2028 is creating a major platform for artists, creative businesses, cultural organisations and institutions across the United Kingdom and Nigeria to develop new partnerships, exchange ideas and showcase creative work to international audiences. Delivered by the British Council in partnership with Nigeria’s Federal Ministry of Art, Culture, Tourism and the Creative Economy, the Season will run from June to December 2028, with legacy activity continuing into 2029. The programme is designed to strengthen the long-term creative relationship between the UK and Nigeria by creating connections between people, organisations and creative industries in both countries. The initiative is particularly significant because it comes a decade after the landmark 2015/16 UK–Nigeria Season, at a time when Nigeria’s creative economy has expanded considerably and the UK and Nigeria are seeking deeper cultural, commercial and institutional connections.

UK–Nigeria Season of Culture 2028: What Is It About?

The UK–Nigeria Season of Culture 2028 is a bilateral cultural initiative bringing together creative communities from both countries.

The Season aims to celebrate the creativity, diversity and cultural heritage of the UK and Nigeria while creating opportunities for collaboration that can continue long after the 2028 programme ends.

According to the British Council, the Season is intended to:

  • Strengthen the creative partnership between the UK and Nigeria.
  • Build lasting professional and institutional connections.
  • Create opportunities for creative collaboration.
  • Open pathways to new markets and audiences.
  • Showcase the depth and diversity of UK and Nigerian creative talent.
  • Support knowledge exchange between creative professionals and institutions.
  • Encourage new artistic commissions and collaborative projects.
  • Strengthen creative infrastructure and systems.
  • Support longer-term relationships that can continue beyond the Season itself.

The wider bilateral initiative is also expected to contribute to skills development, institutional capacity, market access and international connections across the creative economy.

When Will the UK–Nigeria Season of Culture 2028 Take Place?

The main Season will take place from:

June to December 2028

Legacy activities are expected to continue into 2029, meaning that the programme is intended to have an impact beyond the main 2028 calendar.

However, creative professionals and organisations do not have to wait until 2028 to become involved. The programme is already seeking ideas, partnerships and potential collaborations during the preparation and incubation period.

The British Council has described the period before the Season as an opportunity for partner engagement, visiting delegations and programme incubation, helping potential collaborations develop before activities take place in 2028.

Five Key Focus Areas of the Season

The UK–Nigeria Season of Culture 2028 is organised around five major focus areas. Applicants and potential partners should consider how their proposed idea connects with one or more of these areas.

1. Cultural Heritage, Identity and Infrastructure

This focus area recognises the importance of cultural heritage and identity while considering the infrastructure required for the creative sector to thrive.

Projects could explore cultural heritage, storytelling, identity, preservation, cultural spaces, creative infrastructure and related issues.

The emphasis is not simply on presenting culture, but also on strengthening the systems and structures that enable cultural and creative activity to develop sustainably.

2. Market Access and Mutual Growth

The Season also aims to create stronger connections between creative industries and markets in both countries.

This focus area is relevant to organisations, entrepreneurs and creative professionals seeking opportunities to:

  • Reach new audiences.
  • Build international networks.
  • Develop commercial partnerships.
  • Expand into new markets.
  • Connect with buyers, investors or industry professionals.
  • Strengthen the international visibility of their creative work or business.

The broader UK–Nigeria creative partnership has also identified international market access and structured engagement as important areas for strengthening the creative economy.

3. Creative Collaboration and Partnerships

Partnership is at the heart of the Season.

The programme is interested in ideas that bring together people, organisations and institutions from the UK and Nigeria to develop meaningful creative collaborations.

A proposed project does not necessarily need to be completely developed before an expression of interest is submitted. The opportunity specifically welcomes both developed project concepts and early-stage ideas.

If you already have a potential partner in the other country, you can indicate this in your response. If you do not yet have a partner, you can still express your interest and describe the type of collaboration you would like to develop.

4. New Artistic Commissions

The Season will also provide a platform for new creative and artistic work.

This could create possibilities for artists and creative organisations to propose original projects, productions, performances, commissions or other forms of creative activity that contribute to the UK–Nigeria cultural relationship.

The emphasis is on developing ideas capable of creating meaningful artistic and cultural value for audiences in both countries.

5. Research, Policy and Knowledge Exchange

The Season is not limited to performances and exhibitions.

Research, policy discussions, professional learning and knowledge exchange are also part of its vision.

This focus area can be particularly relevant to institutions, researchers, cultural policy professionals, academics, practitioners and organisations working on issues affecting the creative and cultural sectors.

It recognises that long-term creative development requires not only artistic activity but also research, evidence, policy development, institutional learning and the exchange of knowledge between countries.

Which Artforms and Creative Disciplines Are Eligible?

One of the notable features of the UK–Nigeria Season of Culture 2028 is its broad approach to creative disciplines.

The Season is open to all artforms and creative disciplines, rather than restricting participation to a single artistic field.

Potential areas include:

  • Music
  • Film
  • Visual arts
  • Fashion
  • Literature
  • Digital creativity
  • Performing arts
  • Theatre
  • Dance
  • Architecture
  • Gaming
  • Gastronomy
  • Craft
  • Creative technology
  • Other creative and cultural disciplines

This broad scope means that the opportunity may be relevant to both traditional and emerging areas of the creative economy.

The British Council’s wider arts work in Nigeria similarly spans areas including architecture, design, fashion, film, literature, music, theatre, dance and visual arts.

Who Is Being Invited to Get Involved?

The opportunity is aimed at people and organisations within the cultural and creative sectors of both the UK and Nigeria.

The invitation specifically mentions:

  • Artists
  • Creative businesses
  • Cultural organisations
  • Cultural institutions
  • Creative-sector organisations
  • Other relevant institutions and creative practitioners

The British Council is looking for people and organisations with an idea for a project, partnership or collaboration that could contribute to the UK–Nigeria Season of Culture 2028.

You do not necessarily need to have a fully developed project.

The programme welcomes:

  • Fully formed project proposals.
  • Early-stage creative ideas.
  • Potential partnerships.
  • Collaboration concepts.
  • Ideas that could be developed with a partner in the other country.

This makes the expression of interest particularly useful for creative professionals who have a strong concept but may still be exploring how to develop it internationally.

Important: This Is Not a Funding Application

One of the most important points for anyone considering submitting an expression of interest is that this stage is not a funding application.

The purpose of the current Expression of Interest is to:

  1. Gather creative ideas.
  2. Identify potential partners.
  3. Understand what the creative sectors in the UK and Nigeria would like to develop.
  4. Start conversations between potential collaborators.
  5. Explore projects that could form part of the wider Season.
  6. Help shape future programme development.

Therefore, applicants should not approach the EOI as though they are applying for a conventional grant.

Instead, the focus should be on clearly communicating who you are, what you would like to do, how your idea connects to the Season and whether you already have a partner in the other country.

What Should You Include in Your Expression of Interest?

The response should be no more than two pages.

It should cover four essential areas:

1. Who You Are

Introduce yourself, your organisation, institution, creative business or relevant professional background.

Explain your role within the cultural or creative sector and provide enough information for the organisers to understand your experience and relevance to the proposed idea.

2. What You Would Like to Do

Describe your project, partnership or collaboration idea.

This does not have to be a fully developed proposal. If the concept is still at an early stage, explain the idea clearly and describe what you hope to develop.

3. Which Focus Area Your Idea Fits

Explain which of the Season’s five focus areas your idea relates to:

  • Cultural heritage, identity and infrastructure
  • Market access and mutual growth
  • Creative collaboration and partnerships
  • New artistic commissions
  • Research, policy and knowledge exchange

If your project connects with more than one focus area, you can explain those connections.

4. Whether You Have a Partner in the Other Country

State whether you already have a UK or Nigerian partner.

For example, a Nigerian creative organisation could identify a UK institution it already works with, while a UK artist could describe an existing relationship with a Nigerian creative organisation.

If you do not yet have a partner, explain the type of partner or collaboration you would like to develop.

How to Submit Your Expression of Interest

The Expression of Interest should be submitted by email to:UKNigeria.SeasonofCulture@britishcouncil.org

The response should be two pages or fewer and should address the requested information.

The stated deadline is:

14 September 2026

This deadline is important for anyone intending to have their idea considered as part of the current expression-of-interest process.

For official information and updates, visit the https://www.britishcouncil.org.ng/programmes/arts/uk-nigeria-season-culture-2028

Online Information Sessions for Interested Applicants

Two online sessions are being held to help potential participants understand the Expression of Interest process, the Season and what is expected in a response.

Session 1

Date: Monday, 17 August 2026
Time: 11:00 WAT

Session 2

Date: Monday, 7 September 2026
Time: 11:00 WAT

Both sessions cover the same information, so participants can attend one or both.

If you have questions before attending the sessions, you can contact the Season team by email at:UKNigeria.SeasonofCulture@britishcouncil.org

Why Should Creative Professionals Consider Getting Involved?

The UK–Nigeria Season of Culture 2028 presents an opportunity to engage with a major bilateral cultural initiative at an early stage.

For creative professionals and organisations, early involvement can be particularly valuable because the current process is designed to identify ideas and potential partners before the main Season takes place.

Potential areas of value include:

  • Developing UK–Nigeria creative partnerships.
  • Building international professional networks.
  • Exploring new audiences and markets.
  • Developing collaborative creative projects.
  • Connecting creative institutions across both countries.
  • Contributing ideas to a major international cultural programme.
  • Exploring new artistic commissions.
  • Sharing knowledge and expertise.
  • Strengthening international visibility.
  • Building relationships that may continue beyond 2028.

The broader bilateral programme is intended to establish lasting partnerships rather than relationships that end when the Season closes. The British Council has highlighted institutional partnerships, skills development, market access and sustainable creative connections as important elements of the wider initiative.

A Major Opportunity for the UK and Nigerian Creative Economies

The Season arrives at an important period for creative industries in both countries.

Nigeria has developed one of Africa’s most internationally visible creative economies, while the UK has a well-established global creative sector spanning music, film, fashion, theatre, literature, design, gaming and other industries.

The Season provides a structured platform for these ecosystems to connect.

Rather than treating cultural exchange simply as a series of performances or exhibitions, the initiative takes a broader approach that includes creative enterprise, partnerships, infrastructure, policy, research, skills and international market access.

The British Council has also described the 2028 Season as part of a wider effort to strengthen creative systems and production infrastructure, develop skills and leadership, improve access to international markets and create lasting relationships between UK and Nigerian creative institutions.

What Happened During the Previous UK–Nigeria Season?

The 2028 programme builds on the earlier UK–Nigeria Season, which ran from September 2015 to March 2017.

The previous Season demonstrated the potential scale of UK–Nigeria cultural collaboration.

According to the British Council, the 2015/16 Season:

  • Covered nine artforms.
  • Delivered 31 projects.
  • Involved 79 partner organisations.
  • Reached 12 cities.
  • Attracted more than 446,000 attendees to live events.
  • Trained 7,135 artists.

The new Season therefore represents a return to a successful model of cultural exchange, while responding to the significant growth and transformation of the creative sector over the intervening decade.

What Makes the 2028 Season Different?

The creative environment in which the 2028 Season is being developed is significantly different from that of the previous Season.

Digital technology, international streaming, gaming, creative entrepreneurship, social media, emerging technologies and rapidly changing global markets have transformed how artists and creative businesses reach audiences.

The 2028 Season is therefore positioned not only as a celebration of culture but also as a platform for developing stronger creative systems and international relationships.

The British Council has identified areas such as emerging technology, creative infrastructure, professional skills, leadership, international markets and institutional partnerships as part of the wider UK–Nigeria creative collaboration agenda.

Tips for Preparing a Strong Expression of Interest

Although the EOI is limited to two pages, applicants should make every sentence count.

Keep the idea clear

Avoid filling the document with unnecessary background information. Clearly explain what you want to do and why it matters.

Explain the UK–Nigeria connection

Since this is a bilateral Season, make the connection between the two countries clear.

Explain how the project could create meaningful collaboration between Nigerian and UK creative communities, institutions, businesses or audiences.

Connect the idea to a focus area

Do not simply name one of the five focus areas. Explain why your idea belongs there.

Be realistic

If your project is still at an early stage, say so. The EOI specifically welcomes early ideas, so there is no need to present an undeveloped concept as though it is already fully formed.

Highlight your experience

Briefly demonstrate why you or your organisation are well positioned to develop the idea.

Relevant previous projects, partnerships, creative work, audiences or institutional experience can help provide context.

Explain your partnership status

Clearly state whether you already have a partner in the UK or Nigeria.

If you do not, explain what type of partner you would like to work with.

Stay within the two-page limit

The request is for a response of two pages or fewer, so concise and structured communication is important.

Who Can Apply or Express Interest?

The opportunity is intended for the cultural and creative sectors in the United Kingdom and Nigeria.

Potential participants include:

  • Individual artists.
  • Creative businesses.
  • Cultural organisations.
  • Cultural institutions.
  • Creative-sector organisations.
  • Other relevant organisations or practitioners with suitable project or collaboration ideas.

There is no specific race or ethnicity requirement stated in the information provided for this Expression of Interest.

The opportunity is geographically centred on the UK and Nigeria, rather than being presented as a general worldwide opportunity for applicants from every country.

Importantly, eligibility is described in terms of participation in the UK or Nigerian cultural and creative sectors. Therefore, prospective participants should focus on demonstrating their connection to the relevant creative sector and explaining how their proposed idea contributes to UK–Nigeria collaboration.

Is This a Grant or Scholarship?

No.

The current Expression of Interest is explicitly not a funding application. It is a process for gathering ideas, identifying partners and initiating conversations about potential projects for the Season.

Participants should therefore not assume that submitting an EOI automatically provides funding, a grant, a scholarship, employment or another financial award.

Any future project development or support arrangements would depend on subsequent discussions and the programme’s development.

Key Details at a Glance

Opportunity: UK–Nigeria Season of Culture 2028 – Expression of Interest
Main Season: June–December 2028
Legacy activity: Through 2029
Countries: United Kingdom and Nigeria
Creative disciplines: All artforms and creative disciplines
Who can express interest: Artists, organisations, institutions and creative businesses in the UK and Nigeria
Maximum response length: Two pages
Submission method: Email
Submission email: UKNigeria.SeasonofCulture@britishcouncil.org
Deadline: 14 September 2026
Application type: Expression of Interest, not a funding application
Organisers: British Council and Nigeria’s Federal Ministry of Art, Culture, Tourism and the Creative Economy

How to Find More Information

Those interested in participating should consult the official British Council information and follow any updates to the Expression of Interest process.https://www.britishcouncil.org.ng/uknigeria-2015-16-impact-report

More opportunities here, https://opportunitiesforyouth.org

item.content:encoded:
The 2027 Brazil Investment Banking Internship Program offers university students an opportunity to gain practical experience in investment banking with Bank of America in São Paulo, Brazil. The internship is designed for students pursuing disciplines such as Business, Economics, Accounting, Engineering, or related fields who want to build experience in corporate finance, mergers and acquisitions, debt and equity financing, financial analysis, and client advisory.

The position is listed as an Off-cycle Internship under Job ID JR-14454 and is based in São Paulo, Brazil. According to the official Bank of America careers listing, applications are open until December 31, 2027.

For students interested in pursuing careers in investment banking, corporate finance, financial advisory, capital markets, or related areas, this opportunity can provide exposure to the type of transactions and financial solutions that support companies and contribute to the broader global economy.

Opportunity Overview

  • Opportunity: 2027 Brazil Investment Banking Internship Program
  • Position: Investment Banking Intern
  • Organization: Bank of America
  • Location: São Paulo, Brazil
  • Job ID: JR-14454
  • Internship type: Off-cycle internship
  • Work arrangement: In-person or hybrid
  • Working hours: 30 hours per week
  • Minimum age: 18 years
  • Application deadline: December 31, 2027
  • Required language: Fluent English
  • Eligible academic backgrounds: Business, Economics, Accounting, Engineering, and related courses

The official listing confirms that the role is intended for students who are currently studying, attend classes in the morning, and expect to graduate in one year or more.

About the Bank of America Brazil Investment Banking Group

Investment banking is an area of financial services focused on helping companies, institutions, and other organizations make significant financial and strategic decisions.

The Brazil Investment Banking group at Bank of America provides advisory expertise across major corporate finance activities. According to the vacancy announcement, the team works around Mergers and Acquisitions (M&A), Debt underwriting, and Equity underwriting, providing integrated financial solutions to clients.

This means an intern joining the team may be exposed to an environment where financial analysis, corporate strategy, market knowledge, communication, and client service come together.

Mergers and Acquisitions

Mergers and acquisitions involve transactions in which companies combine, acquire other businesses, sell businesses, or restructure ownership.

Investment banking professionals supporting M&A transactions may be involved in activities such as:

  • Financial analysis
  • Company and industry research
  • Valuation
  • Preparation of financial models
  • Analysis of potential transactions
  • Preparation of presentations and transaction materials
  • Supporting due diligence processes
  • Monitoring market developments
  • Preparing information for clients and senior bankers

For an intern, exposure to M&A can provide valuable insight into how major corporate transactions are evaluated and executed.

Debt Underwriting

Debt underwriting involves helping companies and institutions raise capital through debt markets.

Investment banking teams may help clients evaluate financing requirements, structure transactions, assess market conditions, and connect borrowers with investors.

Students interested in corporate finance can therefore gain a better understanding of how businesses finance expansion, acquisitions, operations, and other strategic objectives.

Equity Underwriting

Equity underwriting involves helping companies raise capital through the issuance of shares or other equity-related securities.

This area requires an understanding of financial markets, company performance, valuation, investor considerations, and broader economic conditions.

Exposure to equity transactions can help students understand how businesses access capital markets and how investors evaluate investment opportunities.

Who Is Bank of America Looking For?

The internship is targeted at university students with relevant academic backgrounds and an interest in investment banking.

According to the official vacancy, applicants should meet several important requirements.

1. Students in Relevant Academic Disciplines

Applicants should be studying:

  • Business
  • Economics
  • Accounting
  • Engineering
  • Related courses

This broad academic requirement means that the opportunity is not restricted exclusively to traditional finance or economics students. Students from other related disciplines may also be considered if their academic background and skills are relevant to investment banking.

Engineering students, for example, may bring quantitative, analytical, problem-solving, and technical skills that can be valuable in financial analysis.

2. Morning Shift Students

The vacancy specifically states that applicants should be morning shift students.

This requirement is important because candidates should assess their university timetable before applying. The internship requires availability for 30 hours per week, so applicants need to determine whether their academic schedule can accommodate the required working hours.

3. Students With at Least One Year Remaining Before Graduation

Applicants are expected to graduate in one year or more.

This is an important eligibility condition. Students who are very close to graduation should carefully evaluate whether they satisfy the requirement before submitting an application.

The program is particularly relevant to students who still have sufficient time remaining in their degree to undertake an internship while continuing their studies.

4. Fluent English

Fluent English is mandatory for the position.

Applicants should therefore be comfortable communicating in English in a professional environment.

Strong English communication can be particularly important in investment banking because professionals may need to:

  • Communicate with colleagues
  • Prepare written materials
  • Participate in meetings
  • Understand financial documentation
  • Present analysis
  • Communicate with clients and stakeholders
  • Work in an international business environment

Applicants whose English is not yet at a professional level should consider strengthening their written and spoken communication skills before applying.

5. Availability for 30 Hours Per Week

Candidates must be available to work 30 hours per week.

The internship can be undertaken in an in-person or hybrid format, according to the vacancy information.

Applicants should therefore be prepared to commit substantial weekly time to the internship while continuing their studies.

Key Skills Required for the Investment Banking Internship

Beyond academic qualifications, Bank of America identifies several skills that are relevant to the position.

Strong Knowledge of Corporate Finance

A strong understanding of corporate finance is one of the most important foundations for an investment banking career.

Applicants should ideally understand concepts such as:

  • Financial statements
  • Cash flow
  • Capital structure
  • Cost of capital
  • Valuation
  • Debt financing
  • Equity financing
  • Corporate investment decisions
  • Profitability
  • Financial performance
  • Risk and return

Students who can demonstrate practical understanding rather than simply memorizing definitions may be better prepared for the demands of the role.

Macroeconomic Knowledge

The vacancy also highlights macroeconomic knowledge.

Investment banking decisions do not happen in isolation. Economic conditions can influence companies, investors, capital markets, financing costs, mergers, acquisitions, and investment decisions.

Applicants should therefore develop an understanding of issues such as:

  • Economic growth
  • Inflation
  • Interest rates
  • Monetary policy
  • Fiscal policy
  • Exchange rates
  • Employment
  • Global economic trends
  • Financial market conditions

Keeping up with major economic developments can also help candidates demonstrate genuine interest in financial markets during recruitment.

Strong Communication Skills

Investment banking requires more than numerical ability.

Professionals must communicate complex financial information clearly to colleagues, clients, executives, investors, and other stakeholders.

Strong communication skills can include:

  • Clear writing
  • Professional speaking
  • Presentation skills
  • Active listening
  • Ability to explain complex concepts
  • Attention to detail
  • Professional correspondence
  • Team communication

For students from communication, business, economics, accounting, engineering, and other disciplines, developing the ability to translate technical information into clear business language can be particularly valuable.

Client Focus

The position also emphasizes client focus.

Investment banking is fundamentally a client-oriented business. Bankers work with organizations facing significant strategic, financial, and corporate decisions.

Candidates should therefore demonstrate an understanding of:

  • Professionalism
  • Client service
  • Confidentiality
  • Responsiveness
  • Attention to client requirements
  • Problem-solving
  • Business judgment
  • Teamwork

A candidate who can demonstrate that they understand the importance of delivering high-quality work for clients can strengthen their overall profile.

What Students Can Gain From an Investment Banking Internship

An investment banking internship can be valuable for students who want to understand how the financial sector operates in practice.

Although the exact responsibilities assigned to an intern will depend on the team and business needs, working within an investment banking environment can provide exposure to areas such as financial analysis, corporate transactions, market research, client service, and professional financial communication.

Potential areas of professional development include:

Practical Corporate Finance Exposure

Students can move beyond classroom theory and gain an understanding of how financial concepts are applied in real business situations.

Understanding of Major Corporate Transactions

The Brazil Investment Banking group works across M&A, debt, and equity activities, giving the role a strong connection to major corporate finance transactions.

Professional Workplace Experience

The internship provides an opportunity to work within a major global financial institution and experience professional expectations around communication, teamwork, deadlines, accuracy, and client service.

Financial Market Knowledge

Students can strengthen their understanding of how economic and market conditions affect companies and financial transactions.

Career Development

Experience in investment banking can be relevant to future careers in:

  • Investment banking
  • Corporate finance
  • Private equity
  • Asset management
  • Financial advisory
  • Corporate strategy
  • Capital markets
  • Consulting
  • Commercial banking
  • Financial analysis

The experience can therefore be useful for students considering a long-term career in finance or related business fields.

Why São Paulo Is an Important Location for This Opportunity

São Paulo is one of Brazil’s most important financial and business centers.

For students pursuing financial careers, an internship in São Paulo can provide exposure to Brazil’s corporate and financial environment while allowing participants to work within an international financial institution.

The location is particularly relevant to applicants interested in emerging markets, Latin American finance, multinational corporations, and cross-border business.

Applicants who are not currently based in São Paulo should pay close attention to the position’s in-person or hybrid requirements and determine whether they can realistically meet the workplace expectations.

Age Requirement

The vacancy specifies that applicants must be at least 18 years old.

Candidates who are below 18 should therefore not assume that they qualify simply because they meet the academic requirements.

Work Arrangement

The internship offers an in-person or hybrid format, with a commitment of 30 hours per week.

The flexibility of a hybrid arrangement may be useful for some students, but applicants should not interpret “hybrid” as meaning that the internship is fully remote.

Candidates should be prepared to participate in the working arrangement required by the employer.

Application Deadline

The stated application deadline for the 2027 Brazil Investment Banking Internship Program is:

December 31, 2027

Applicants are encouraged not to wait until the final day to submit their applications. Recruitment processes can involve multiple stages, and preparing a strong application in advance gives candidates more time to review their information and ensure that all required materials are complete.

The official Bank of America careers page currently lists December 31, 2027 as the application deadline.

How to Apply

Interested applicants should apply through the official Bank of America careers platform.

When applying, candidates should carefully review the official vacancy requirements and provide accurate academic, professional, and personal information.

Applicants should ensure that their application clearly demonstrates:

  1. Their current academic program.
  2. Their expected graduation date.
  3. Their relevant academic knowledge.
  4. Their interest in investment banking.
  5. Their understanding of corporate finance.
  6. Their communication abilities.
  7. Their analytical and problem-solving skills.
  8. Their availability to work 30 hours per week.
  9. Their English proficiency.
  10. Their suitability for an in-person or hybrid position in São Paulo.
