How to Make Your Application Stronger

Meeting the minimum requirements is only one part of a competitive application. Candidates should also make an effort to demonstrate why they are genuinely interested in investment banking.

Tailor Your Resume

Avoid submitting a generic resume that does not highlight finance-related capabilities.

Where applicable, emphasize:

  • Financial analysis
  • Economics
  • Accounting
  • Corporate finance
  • Research
  • Data analysis
  • Business projects
  • Leadership
  • Teamwork
  • Presentations
  • Communication
  • Problem-solving
  • Relevant internships
  • Extracurricular activities

Highlight Relevant Coursework

Students should consider highlighting courses relevant to investment banking, including:

  • Corporate Finance
  • Financial Accounting
  • Economics
  • Statistics
  • Business Mathematics
  • Investment Analysis
  • Financial Markets
  • Business Strategy
  • Valuation

Demonstrate Analytical Ability

Investment banking is highly analytical, so applicants should identify experiences where they have analyzed information, solved complex problems, interpreted data, or made evidence-based recommendations.

This does not necessarily have to come from previous employment. Academic projects, case competitions, student organizations, research projects, and other activities can also demonstrate analytical ability.

Demonstrate Communication Skills

Because communication is specifically identified as an important skill for the role, candidates should make sure their application reflects strong written communication.

A resume that is clear, logically organized, concise, and free from avoidable errors can help demonstrate professionalism.

Research Bank of America and Investment Banking

Candidates should understand the organization and the business area they are applying to.

Before an interview or assessment, applicants should research:

  • Bank of America’s business operations
  • Investment banking
  • M&A
  • Debt markets
  • Equity markets
  • Current economic conditions
  • Brazil’s financial environment
  • Major trends affecting corporate finance

This preparation can help candidates provide stronger and more informed responses during recruitment.

Frequently Asked Questions

What is the 2027 Brazil Investment Banking Internship Program?

It is an off-cycle Investment Banking Intern position with Bank of America in São Paulo, Brazil, designed for students pursuing Business, Economics, Accounting, Engineering, or related courses.

Where is the internship located?

The position is based in São Paulo, Brazil.

Is the internship remote?

No. The official listing specifies an in-person or hybrid internship format.

How many hours per week does the internship require?

Applicants must be available to work 30 hours per week.

What degree programs are eligible?

The vacancy identifies Business, Economics, Accounting, Engineering, and related courses as relevant academic backgrounds.

Do I need to speak English?

Yes. Fluent English is mandatory according to the official job posting.

What age do I need to be?

Applicants must be at least 18 years old.

When is the application deadline?

The stated deadline is December 31, 2027.

What job ID should applicants look for?

The position is listed under JR-14454.

Is this a graduate job?

No. It is an internship opportunity for current students. Applicants are expected to have one year or more remaining before graduation.

Important Note for International Applicants

The information provided in the official vacancy confirms the academic, language, age, schedule, and work-format requirements, but applicants from outside Brazil should carefully review the official application and employment requirements before applying.

International candidates should not automatically assume that being academically eligible means they are authorized to undertake an internship in Brazil. Any applicable immigration, work authorization, residency, or local employment requirements should be independently confirmed through the appropriate official channels.

The official vacancy should remain the primary source for the most current application requirements.

Conclusion

The 2027 Brazil Investment Banking Internship Program at Bank of America is a valuable opportunity for students who want to begin building a career in investment banking and corporate finance. Based in São Paulo, the internship offers exposure to a financial environment focused on major activities including Mergers and Acquisitions, debt underwriting, and equity underwriting.

The opportunity is particularly suited to students studying Business, Economics, Accounting, Engineering, or related disciplines who have a strong interest in corporate finance and financial markets. Candidates must be at least 18 years old, fluent in English, attend classes in the morning, expect to graduate in one year or more, and be available to work 30 hours per week in an in-person or hybrid format.

With the application deadline set for December 31, 2027, interested students have an opportunity to prepare their resumes, strengthen their corporate finance and macroeconomic knowledge, research the investment banking industry, and submit a carefully tailored application.

Students who are serious about entering investment banking should view this type of internship not simply as a temporary placement, but as an opportunity to develop technical knowledge, professional communication skills, financial-market awareness, and practical experience that can support future careers across finance and business.

item.content:encoded:
The ARES International Training Scholarships 2027–2028 offer an opportunity for qualified graduates and working professionals from selected developing and partner countries to undertake specialised higher education and professional training in Belgium.

The programme is administered by the Académie de Recherche et d’Enseignement Supérieur (ARES) and supports specialised academic and professional programmes within the higher education system of the Wallonia-Brussels Federation in Belgium. For the 2027–2028 call, applicants can choose from one specialised bachelor’s programme, eight specialised master’s programmes, and one continuing education programme.

Applications opened on 3 August 2026, and the application deadline is Friday, 18 September 2026 at 12:00 noon Belgian time (UTC+1). Applicants are strongly advised to begin the process early because the application requires account creation, documentation, eligibility checks and submission through the ARES GIRAF platform.

ARES International Training Scholarships 2027–2028 at a Glance

  • Host country: Belgium
  • Organiser: Académie de Recherche et d’Enseignement Supérieur (ARES)
  • Academic year: 2027–2028
  • Application opening date: 3 August 2026
  • Application deadline: 18 September 2026 at 12:00 noon Belgian time (UTC+1)
  • Study location: Institutions within the Wallonia-Brussels Federation
  • Available programmes: 1 specialised bachelor’s degree, 8 specialised master’s degrees and 1 continuing education programme
  • Duration: Up to 12 months for the specialised bachelor’s and master’s programmes; up to 6 months for continuing education
  • Eligible applicants: Residents and workers from 32 eligible partner countries, with a special provision for Palestinian nationals
  • Application platform: ARES GIRAF
  • Application limit: One programme per applicant
  • Funding: International travel, living/subsistence support, applicable tuition fees, insurance and certain visa-related or other eligible costs

What Are the ARES International Training Scholarships?

The ARES International Training Scholarships are designed to strengthen the academic knowledge, technical expertise and professional capacity of people from eligible partner countries.

Rather than being a general scholarship open to applicants from every country, the programme targets candidates from a defined group of partner countries. Applicants are expected to demonstrate both academic preparation and professional experience relevant to the programme they wish to pursue.

The 2027–2028 call provides specialised training in areas connected to major development and professional challenges, including:

  • Human rights
  • Public health
  • International and development economics
  • Microfinance
  • Food-chain safety
  • Supply-chain management
  • Cybersecurity
  • Health-risk management
  • Cultural conservation and collections management
  • Disaster and risk management

The programme therefore has potential relevance to professionals working in government, development organisations, NGOs, healthcare, finance, supply chains, technology, public administration, humanitarian work, research, education and other related fields.

Programmes Available Under the ARES 2027–2028 Call

Applicants should carefully examine the admission requirements of their preferred programme before beginning the application because academic and professional requirements can differ between programmes.

1. Specialised Bachelor’s Degree

The 2027–2028 call includes one specialised bachelor’s programme:

Specialised Bachelor’s in Digital Integrated Supply Chain

This programme is particularly relevant to candidates interested in modern supply-chain systems, logistics, digital transformation, procurement, international business and integrated supply-chain management.

The programme may be particularly attractive to professionals whose careers involve logistics, procurement, supply-chain operations, business management, international development or related areas.

The specialised bachelor’s programme has a maximum duration of 12 months.

2. Eight Specialised Master’s Programmes

Applicants can also choose from eight specialised master’s programmes covering a broad range of development-oriented disciplines.

The available programmes include:

  1. Specialised Master’s in Human Rights
  2. Specialised Master’s in Integrated Health Risk Management
  3. Specialised Master in International and Development Economics
  4. Advanced Master in Microfinance
  5. Specialised Master’s in Public Health Sciences – Analysis and Evaluation of International Health Policies, Programmes and Systems
  6. Specialised Master’s in Food Chain Safety Management
  7. Specialised Master’s in Preventive Conservation and Collections Management
  8. Specialised Master’s in Risk and Disaster Management in the Anthropocene Era

These programmes provide opportunities for professionals to deepen their expertise in fields that have significant relevance to sustainable development, public policy, health systems, economic development, food security, cultural heritage, disaster preparedness and humanitarian responses.

The specialised master’s programmes have a maximum duration of 12 months.

3. Continuing Education Programme

The call also includes a continuing education opportunity:

Certificate in Cybersecurity Operations and Risk Governance

The programme focuses on cybersecurity operations and the governance of digital risks. It may be particularly relevant for professionals working in information technology, cybersecurity, digital governance, risk management and related fields.

The continuing education programme has a maximum duration of six months.

Who Can Apply for the ARES Scholarships?

The ARES scholarships have specific eligibility requirements. Meeting one requirement alone does not necessarily make an applicant eligible. Candidates should satisfy the residency, employment, academic, professional experience and programme-specific admission requirements.

1. Applicants Must Be Connected to an Eligible Country

Candidates must be permanent residents and workers in one of the 32 eligible countries.

There is a specific exception for Palestinian nationals, who may qualify even when they do not reside in one of the 32 listed countries.

This means that simply holding nationality from an eligible country may not be sufficient in every case. The call specifically refers to residence and employment requirements, so applicants should carefully review their circumstances before submitting an application.

2. Applicants Must Hold an Appropriate Higher Education Qualification

Candidates must have an appropriate higher education qualification and satisfy the admission requirements of the programme they select.

The relevant qualification must generally have been obtained no more than 20 years before the start of the programme.

The maximum period can be extended by one additional year for each childbirth and/or adoption, according to the eligibility conditions provided in the call.

Applicants should therefore examine the academic requirements of their selected programme rather than assuming that every university degree will automatically qualify them.

3. Professional Experience Is Required

Applicants must demonstrate at least two years of relevant professional experience in one of the eligible countries.

The experience must have been acquired after completion of the most recent graduate degree and before the application deadline.

This requirement makes the scholarship particularly relevant to working professionals who already have experience in their field and want to acquire specialised international training that can strengthen their contribution to their organisations and communities.

4. Language Proficiency

Applicants must complete their application in the language in which their chosen programme is taught.

Candidates are expected to demonstrate good written and spoken command of the relevant teaching language.

Applicants should therefore check the language requirements of their specific programme before applying.

The scholarship information also notes that having a basic knowledge of French can be helpful for integration into everyday life in Belgium, even where the programme itself may have different language requirements.

5. Applicants Can Apply for Only One Programme

One of the important rules of the ARES call is that an applicant may apply for only one programme.

Applicants should therefore research the available courses carefully before submitting their application.

Choosing a programme should involve considering:

  • Academic background
  • Professional experience
  • Career objectives
  • Programme admission requirements
  • Language requirements
  • Relevance to the applicant’s professional field
  • Long-term career plans

Submitting applications for multiple programmes is not an appropriate strategy under this call.

Which Countries Are Eligible?

The ARES International Training Scholarships are open to applicants connected to 32 eligible partner countries across Africa, Asia, Southeast Asia, South America and the Caribbean.

Eligible African Countries

The African countries included in the call are:

  • Benin
  • Burkina Faso
  • Burundi
  • Cameroon
  • Democratic Republic of the Congo
  • Ethiopia
  • Guinea
  • Côte d’Ivoire
  • Kenya
  • Madagascar
  • Mali
  • Morocco
  • Mozambique
  • Niger
  • Rwanda
  • Senegal
  • South Africa
  • Tanzania
  • Tunisia
  • Uganda
  • Zimbabwe

Eligible Countries in South America and the Caribbean

The eligible countries listed in this region are:

  • Bolivia
  • Cuba
  • Ecuador
  • Haiti
  • Peru

Eligible Southeast Asian Countries

The eligible Southeast Asian countries are:

  • Cambodia
  • Indonesia
  • Nepal
  • Philippines
  • Vietnam

Eligible Asian Country

  • Palestine

Therefore, applicants from Kenya, Uganda, Tanzania, Rwanda, Ethiopia, South Africa, Mozambique, Zimbabwe and the other listed partner countries can potentially apply, provided they satisfy all other eligibility requirements.

Importantly, this is not a scholarship open to all African countries. Applicants should check the official country list before investing time in preparing an application.

What Does the Scholarship Cover?

The ARES International Training Scholarships provide substantial financial support to successful applicants.

The support listed in the call includes several major categories.

International Travel Expenses

Scholarship recipients receive support for international travel expenses associated with their studies or training in Belgium.

This can significantly reduce one of the major financial barriers faced by international applicants who need to travel to Europe for their programme.

Subsistence Allowance

The scholarship includes a subsistence allowance to help recipients meet living expenses during their period of study or training.

This is particularly important for international students who may otherwise need to finance accommodation, food and other daily expenses independently.

Tuition Fees

For the specialised bachelor’s and specialised master’s programmes, the scholarship includes support for tuition fees.

This means successful recipients can undertake their eligible programme without having to independently finance the applicable tuition costs covered by the scholarship.

Visa-Related Expenses

For specialised bachelor’s and specialised master’s recipients, the scholarship can cover exceptional costs associated with visa applications, subject to the conditions of the programme and scholarship.

This provides additional financial support during the relocation process.

Insurance

Insurance costs are also included in the scholarship support.

This provides an additional layer of financial protection for recipients while they are undertaking their programme in Belgium.

Continuing Education Support

For the continuing education programme, the financial package includes indirect mission expenses, alongside the applicable scholarship support described in the call.

Because funding arrangements can differ depending on the programme type, applicants should consult the official call documentation for the exact financial conditions applicable to their selected programme.

How Long Are the ARES Programmes?

The duration depends on the type of programme selected.

Specialised Bachelor’s and Master’s Programmes

The specialised bachelor’s and specialised master’s programmes have a maximum duration of:

12 months

Continuing Education

The continuing education programme has a maximum duration of:

6 months

Applicants should distinguish these programmes from conventional multi-year undergraduate or master’s programmes. The ARES International Training call is focused on specialised training and academic programmes designed to strengthen the expertise of candidates who already possess relevant educational and professional backgrounds.

How to Apply for the ARES International Training Scholarships 2027–2028

Applications are submitted electronically through the ARES GIRAF platform.

The application process involves several stages.

Step 1: Create or Access Your GIRAF Account

Applicants who already have a GIRAF account created and validated by ARES can log in using their existing account.

Candidates who do not have a validated GIRAF account must complete the account creation request process.

It is advisable to do this well before the deadline because applicants should not leave account creation and validation until the final hours of the application period.

Step 2: Access the International Training Application

After logging into GIRAF, navigate to:

Competitive Calls

Then select:

Application – International Training 2027–2028

Applicants should click the application button only once, according to the application instructions.

Step 3: Complete the Application Form

Applicants should carefully complete all required sections of the form.

Certain fields marked with an asterisk are mandatory and must be completed before the application can initially be saved.

The system allows applicants to work on the application over multiple sessions.

This means candidates do not necessarily need to complete everything in one sitting.

Step 4: Save Your Application as a Draft

If an applicant needs additional time to gather information or documents, the form can be saved as a draft.

To continue a saved application, applicants should go to:

Competitive Calls → My Tasks

They can then select the relevant application and click:

Open

The applicant can continue editing the form as long as it remains a draft and has not been submitted.

Step 5: Review the Application Carefully

Before submission, applicants should check:

  • Personal information
  • Academic qualifications
  • Employment history
  • Professional experience
  • Programme selection
  • Language information
  • Supporting documentation
  • Eligibility information
  • Contact details
  • Any programme-specific requirements

A careful final review is important because errors or missing information can affect the application.

Step 6: Submit the Application

Once everything has been completed and reviewed, the applicant can select:

Submit my application

After submission, the application will appear under:

Competitive Calls → My Submitted Applications

A crucial point is that an application cannot be modified after it has been submitted.

Applicants should therefore avoid submitting prematurely.

Important Application Deadline

The deadline for the ARES International Training Scholarships 2027–2028 is:

Friday, 18 September 2026 at 12:00 noon Belgian time (UTC+1).

Applications opened on 3 August 2026.

Applicants should not wait until the final day to create their GIRAF account, upload documents or submit the application.

Because the deadline is based on Belgian time, international applicants should also account for the time difference between Belgium and their home country.

Important Documents and Preparation

Although exact documentation can depend on the selected programme, applicants should be prepared to provide evidence supporting their eligibility and application.

Potentially relevant materials include:

  • Academic certificates and diplomas
  • Academic transcripts
  • Evidence of professional experience
  • Employment information
  • Proof of residence
  • Proof of nationality
  • Language-related documentation where applicable
  • Programme-specific documents
  • Recommendation or reference information where required
  • Any additional documentation requested by the selected programme

Applicants should use the official ARES candidate guide and call documentation to determine exactly what must be submitted.

It is also advisable to ensure that documents are clear, valid and prepared in the required language or format before beginning the final submission process.

How to Strengthen Your ARES Scholarship Application

Meeting the minimum requirements does not automatically guarantee selection. Applicants should therefore approach the application strategically.

1. Select a Programme That Matches Your Background

Do not choose a programme simply because it is fully funded.

Your academic background and professional experience should make sense in relation to your chosen field.

For example, someone with professional experience in logistics, procurement, operations or supply-chain management may find the Digital Integrated Supply Chain programme particularly relevant.

Similarly, someone working in public health should carefully examine the public-health and health-risk programmes.

2. Connect Your Professional Experience to Your Career Goals

Your professional experience should demonstrate why the programme is useful for your career.

Explain the skills you have already developed and identify the knowledge gaps that the programme will help you address.

A strong application should create a logical connection between:

Past experience → Current professional responsibilities → Selected programme → Future impact

3. Demonstrate Development Impact

Because the programme is designed around international cooperation and capacity building, applicants should clearly demonstrate how advanced training could contribute to their institution, sector or wider community after completion.

Think beyond personal advancement.

Consider how the knowledge gained in Belgium could be applied to:

  • Improve organisational systems
  • Strengthen public services
  • Develop innovative programmes
  • Improve professional practices
  • Address development challenges
  • Build institutional capacity
  • Transfer knowledge to colleagues
  • Support sustainable development

4. Check Programme-Specific Admission Requirements

One of the most important steps is to review the detailed admission requirements for the programme you intend to select.

Different programmes can have different academic prerequisites and professional expectations.

A candidate who meets the general ARES requirements may still fail to meet the admission conditions of a particular programme.

5. Start Early

Do not treat the deadline as the date to begin the application.

A better approach is to:

  1. Check eligibility.
  2. Research the programmes.
  3. Select one suitable programme.
  4. Create and validate your GIRAF account.
  5. Gather supporting documents.
  6. Complete the application.
  7. Review the information.
  8. Submit before the deadline.

Starting early also gives you time to address technical or documentation problems.

Why This Scholarship Is Valuable

The ARES International Training Scholarships can provide more than financial assistance.

For successful candidates, studying or undertaking professional training in Belgium can provide opportunities to:

  • Gain specialised international academic training
  • Develop advanced professional expertise
  • Study in a European higher education environment
  • Build international professional networks
  • Learn from specialists and academic institutions
  • Strengthen career prospects
  • Acquire knowledge that can be applied in the home country
  • Gain exposure to international approaches and practices
  • Develop skills relevant to development challenges
  • Expand professional and academic perspectives

For mid-career professionals, the opportunity can be especially valuable because it combines international exposure with specialised training rather than simply providing a general academic qualification.

Key Mistakes Applicants Should Avoid

Applicants should be particularly careful to avoid the following mistakes:

Applying for More Than One Programme

The call permits applicants to apply for only one programme.

Ignoring the Residency and Employment Requirement

Being from an eligible country does not mean every applicant automatically qualifies. The residency and employment conditions should be carefully checked.

Applying Without the Required Professional Experience

The call requires at least two years of relevant professional experience under the stated conditions.

Choosing a Programme Without Checking Academic Requirements

Every programme can have specific admission requirements.

Submitting an Incomplete Application

Missing information or documentation can weaken an application or make it ineligible.

Waiting Until the Deadline

Technical issues, account validation, missing documents or last-minute errors can create serious problems.

Forgetting That Submitted Applications Cannot Be Edited

Applicants should review everything carefully before clicking the final submission button.

Who Should Consider Applying?

The opportunity may be particularly suitable for:

  • Professionals from eligible developing and partner countries
  • Graduates seeking advanced specialised training
  • Mid-career professionals who want to strengthen their expertise
  • Professionals working in development-related fields
  • Public-sector employees
  • NGO and civil-society professionals
  • Health professionals
  • Supply-chain and logistics professionals
  • Economists and development practitioners
  • Human-rights professionals
  • Financial and microfinance specialists
  • Food-safety professionals
  • Disaster-risk and humanitarian practitioners
  • Cybersecurity and technology professionals
  • Professionals working in cultural heritage and collections management

However, applicants should not rely solely on their professional field. They must also satisfy the official ARES eligibility requirements and the admission requirements of their selected programme.

APPLY HERE

Application Resources

Applicants should consult the official ARES application information, candidate guidance and call documentation before submitting.

The ARES candidate guide should be used to understand the GIRAF application process and submission requirements.

Applicants should also consult the official 2027–2028 call reference document for the authoritative eligibility, programme and funding conditions.

For questions concerning the scholarship call, the provided contact is: Maryvonne Aubry Email: scholarships-cooperation@ares-ac.be

Visit HERE to learn more about the ARES International Training Scholarships 2027–2028 in Belgium.

Final Thoughts

The ARES International Training Scholarships 2027–2028 represent a significant opportunity for qualified professionals and graduates from 32 eligible partner countries to undertake specialised academic or professional training in Belgium with substantial financial support.

The programme stands out because of the range of disciplines available. Applicants can pursue training connected to human rights, public health, international and development economics, microfinance, food-chain safety, cultural conservation, disaster and risk management, supply-chain management and cybersecurity.

The scholarship is particularly suited to candidates who already have relevant academic qualifications and professional experience and who can clearly demonstrate how specialised international training will contribute to their professional development and wider impact.

For eligible applicants, the most important next step is to verify the requirements of the specific programme they wish to pursue, prepare the required documentation and establish or validate their GIRAF account well before the deadline.

Application deadline: 18 September 2026 at 12:00 noon Belgian time (UTC+1).

Applicants should submit their applications before the deadline and remember that once an application is submitted, it can no longer be modified. Always verify the latest requirements and instructions through the official ARES documentation before submitting.

item.content:encoded:
The Aga Khan University (AKU) is inviting students to apply for its Fall 2026 Virtual Internship Programme (AKU-VIP), an opportunity designed to help students gain practical professional experience, develop global perspectives, and build valuable career skills through fully virtual internships.

The Fall 2026 cycle features a range of placements across the Aga Khan Development Network, including opportunities in education, school improvement, health sciences, communications, research, and partnerships.

Students do not need to relocate or obtain a visa to participate. Through virtual project-based work, participants can collaborate with professionals in different countries while gaining experience that complements their academic studies and future career goals.

About the AKU Virtual Internship Programme

The Aga Khan University Virtual Internship Programme (AKU-VIP) provides students with structured virtual work placements with organizations within the Aga Khan Development Network.

The programme is designed around the idea of gaining global experience while remaining locally based. Students can contribute to meaningful projects, interact with professional mentors, and develop an understanding of working in an international environment without the costs associated with international travel and relocation.

Placements are available across 14 or more countries within the Aga Khan Development Network, giving participants exposure to organizations and professionals working across different regions and sectors.

The programme combines flexibility with structured professional experience, making it suitable for students who want to develop their careers while continuing with their academic or personal commitments.

Fall 2026 Internship Opportunities

For the Fall 2026 cycle, students can apply for several virtual positions. Among the available placements are opportunities in education and school improvement.

1. Education Intern

The Education Intern position is offered through the Centre for Innovation in Medical Education (CIME) at Aga Khan University in Nairobi, Kenya.

This opportunity is particularly relevant to students interested in education, learning, innovation, research, and the development of effective educational approaches.

The placement falls under the Health Sciences internship stream and provides students with an opportunity to gain professional experience while contributing to work connected to education and innovation.

2. School Improvement Programme Intern

The School Improvement Programme Intern position is with Aga Khan Schools and is based with the Head Office in London, United Kingdom.

This placement is particularly relevant to students interested in education, school improvement, teaching and learning, education systems, and programmes designed to strengthen school performance.

The internship provides an opportunity to gain exposure to professional work focused on improving educational outcomes and supporting school development.

Other Fall 2026 Virtual Internship Positions

In addition to the education-focused opportunities, the Fall 2026 cycle includes other placements across different fields.

Available positions listed for the cycle include:

  • Communications Research Intern – Aga Khan Schools, Geneva, Switzerland
  • Research Intern – Aga Khan University, Community Health Sciences, Karachi, Pakistan
  • School Improvement Programme Intern – Aga Khan Schools, London, UK
  • Partnerships and Research Intern – Aga Khan University, Centre of Excellence Women and Child Health, Nairobi, Kenya
  • Education Intern – Aga Khan University, Centre for Innovation in Medical Education, Nairobi, Kenya

Students should review the individual placement descriptions and Terms of Reference before applying because each position may have specific requirements, responsibilities, and application instructions.

What Does the Virtual Internship Involve?

AKU-VIP internships are designed around project-based professional work. Rather than simply observing an organization, interns contribute to projects and activities connected to their selected placement.

The internships run for 12 weeks, with students expected to commit at least 15 hours per week.

This structure gives students an opportunity to balance the internship with their academic and personal responsibilities while still gaining meaningful professional exposure.

Depending on the placement, students may work on areas such as research, education, communications, project management, data analysis, healthcare, partnerships, and other professional activities.

Why Apply for the AKU Virtual Internship Programme?

Gain International Work Experience

Students can gain experience working with organizations connected to an international development network without having to travel abroad.

This can help participants understand professional practices in different countries and develop confidence working in multicultural environments.

Develop Practical Career Skills

The programme provides hands-on experience through project-based assignments. Students can develop skills that complement their academic qualifications and prepare them for future employment or further study.

Build a Global Perspective

Working virtually with professionals and organizations across different regions can expose participants to different approaches to problem-solving, education, development, research, and professional collaboration.

Connect With Professionals

The programme provides opportunities to interact with mentors and professionals working across the Aga Khan Development Network.

These connections can help students expand their professional networks and gain insight into different career pathways.

Flexible Virtual Format

Because the programme is virtual, students can participate without relocating to the country where their host organization is located.

The programme is designed to provide structure while maintaining flexibility around students’ academic and personal commitments.

Strengthen Your CV

Completing a structured international virtual internship can provide students with practical experience to include on their CVs, LinkedIn profiles, scholarship applications, graduate school applications, and future job applications.

Programme Duration and Commitment

Each AKU-VIP internship lasts for 12 weeks.

Participants are expected to dedicate at least 15 hours per week to their internship activities.

The virtual structure allows students to participate remotely while contributing to projects with their selected host institution.

Applicants should therefore ensure that they can make the required time commitment before applying.

How the Application Process Works

The AKU Virtual Internship Programme follows a structured application process.

Step 1: Online Application

Students first submit an online application for their preferred internship placement.

Applicants should carefully review the requirements and Terms of Reference for the position before submitting their application.

Step 2: Virtual Interview

Applicants who progress through the selection process may be invited to participate in a virtual interview.

This gives the host organization an opportunity to assess the applicant’s suitability for the placement.

Step 3: Acceptance and Payment

Successful applicants receive an acceptance and proceed with the required payment process.

Applicants should review the programme’s official fee information before applying so they understand the financial requirements associated with participation.

Step 4: Internship Start

Once the process is completed, accepted students begin their 12-week virtual internship with their selected host organization.

Who Should Apply?

The programme is suitable for students who want to gain practical experience and develop their professional skills while participating remotely.

Students with interests in areas such as the following may find the available Fall 2026 placements particularly relevant:

  • Education
  • School improvement
  • Research
  • Health sciences
  • Communications
  • Partnerships
  • Project management
  • International development
  • Professional and career development

Applicants should also be prepared to work independently, communicate effectively online, meet deadlines, and dedicate the required hours each week to their internship.

Because each placement has its own Terms of Reference, students should check the specific requirements of their preferred position before applying.

Fall 2026 Deadline

The application deadline for the Fall 2026 Virtual Internship Programme is:

August 30, 2026

Students interested in participating should submit their applications before the deadline and allow sufficient time to review their preferred placement and prepare their application.

How to Apply

Interested students can learn more about the Aga Khan University Virtual Internship Programme and access the application through the official programme website.

Application Website: www.aku.edu/vip

Students can also review the available Fall 2026 placements and their individual Terms of Reference through the official Aga Khan University website before applying.

Important Information for Applicants

Before submitting an application, prospective applicants should:

  • Review the available internship positions carefully.
  • Identify a placement that matches their academic background and career interests.
  • Read the Terms of Reference for their preferred position.
  • Check the specific requirements and responsibilities of the placement.
  • Confirm that they can commit at least 15 hours per week for 12 weeks.
  • Prepare their application materials in advance.
  • Take note of the programme’s payment requirements.
  • Submit their application before the August 30, 2026 deadline.

Conclusion

The Aga Khan University Fall 2026 Virtual Internship Programme offers students the opportunity to gain practical international experience without leaving their home country.

With placements available across education, school improvement, research, health sciences, communications, and other fields, AKU-VIP can help students develop practical skills, expand their professional networks, gain global perspectives, and strengthen their career profiles.

For students interested specifically in education, the Education Intern and School Improvement Programme Intern positions provide opportunities to contribute to work related to education and school development while gaining valuable professional experience.

The Fall 2026 application deadline is August 30, 2026.

item.content:encoded:
Team4Tech is inviting education-focused nonprofits and NGOs operating in Africa to apply for its Experience AI Cohort, a free, structured learning programme designed to help nonprofit staff and teachers build practical knowledge and confidence in artificial intelligence and machine learning.

Developed by the Raspberry Pi Foundation and Google DeepMind, Experience AI provides research-based educational resources for teachers and students aged 11–14. Through the three-month cohort, selected organizations will participate in live virtual sessions, self-paced learning, coaching, and peer-learning activities to develop the skills needed to introduce AI literacy to their learning communities.

About the Experience AI Cohort

The programme will run from September through early December 2026 and will support participating NGOs in understanding the foundations of AI and implementing Experience AI lessons with teachers and learners.

Participants will explore how AI is used in everyday life, how computers learn from data, and how issues such as limited datasets can contribute to bias. They will also gain practical experience training and testing machine learning models and learn strategies for identifying misinformation in an increasingly AI-driven world.

The programme will also introduce participants to AI-related career pathways, helping educators prepare young people for a future where AI and digital skills are increasingly important.

What Participants Will Learn

Through the Experience AI programme, participants will:

  • Explore how artificial intelligence is used in the world today.
  • Understand how computers learn from data using machine learning.
  • Discover how limited datasets can contribute to bias.
  • Train and test a machine learning model to address a real-world problem.
  • Develop strategies for distinguishing facts from false information in the age of AI.
  • Learn about careers and opportunities related to artificial intelligence.
  • Build confidence in delivering practical AI learning experiences.

What Participating NGOs Will Receive

Selected organizations will have access to:

  • Research-based Experience AI resources and coursework.
  • Live virtual learning and peer-learning sessions.
  • Self-paced learning modules.
  • Coaching and facilitation from Team4Tech.
  • Opportunities to strengthen staff knowledge and practical AI skills.
  • An implementation stipend upon successful completion of the required course activities.

The stipend can be used to support the organization’s implementation of the learning and strategies developed through the cohort.

Who Can Apply?

The opportunity is intended for education nonprofits and NGOs operating in Africa that are interested in using Experience AI lessons to strengthen AI literacy among teachers and learners.

Participating organizations are expected to nominate 2–4 staff members who can commit approximately 15–20 total hours over three months.

Organizations should also be prepared to:

  • Complete asynchronous learning activities and assignments.
  • Attend six live virtual sessions focused on peer learning, sharing, and feedback.
  • Complete pre- and post-cohort surveys.
  • Complete a follow-up survey approximately 4–6 months after participation.
  • Develop plans for implementing Experience AI within their organization and learner community.

Participants should also be comfortable completing coursework and participating in coaching sessions in English.

Who Will Benefit?

The programme is particularly relevant to organizations working with teachers and young learners aged 11–14.

By participating, NGOs can build their internal capacity to introduce young people to foundational AI concepts, responsible use of technology, machine learning, bias, misinformation, and AI-related careers.

Organizations will also have the opportunity to share their learning with additional staff and teachers. Applicants are asked to indicate how many additional educators they expect to train on Experience AI lessons within the following 6–12 months.

Expected Impact

Experience AI can help participating organizations strengthen their education programmes by giving educators practical tools and knowledge to introduce AI concepts in an accessible way.

Through the cohort, participating NGOs can develop strategies for integrating AI literacy into their existing programmes, help teachers become more confident in discussing AI with students, and give learners opportunities to understand how AI systems work rather than simply using AI tools.

The programme can therefore contribute to stronger digital skills, AI awareness, critical thinking, and career readiness among young people.

Important Dates

Application Deadline: September 4, 2026

Selection Decisions: September 16–18, 2026

Programme Period: September 2026 – early December 2026

Up to 10 NGOs operating in Africa are expected to participate in the cohort.

How to Apply

Interested NGOs should complete the Experience AI Cohort application form before the September 4, 2026 deadline.

Application: Apply for the Experience AI Cohort

For questions specifically about the Experience AI cohort, applicants can contact Michelle Mwangi at michelle@team4tech.org. For other questions, contact community@team4tech.org.

Conclusion

The Team4Tech Experience AI Cohort 2026 provides African education nonprofits with an opportunity to strengthen their staff capacity in artificial intelligence and bring practical AI learning experiences to teachers and young people.

With free coursework, live sessions, coaching, research-based resources, and an implementation stipend, the programme can help participating organizations take meaningful steps toward building AI-ready learning communities.

Discover  more opportunities on the OFY Webpage.

item.content:encoded:
The Truist 2027 Credit Internship Program offers an opportunity for ambitious university students to gain practical experience in financial services while developing their knowledge of credit, risk management, banking, and business operations.

The internship is part of Truist’s broad-based early-career internship programme, which combines education, professional exposure, and practical work experience. Through the Credit track, interns are connected with lines of business within Wholesale Banking, giving them an opportunity to develop an understanding of the day-to-day responsibilities involved in areas such as Commercial & Corporate Banking, Specialized Industries and Wholesale Payments.

The programme is designed for students who are interested in building careers in financial services and who want to complement their university education with hands-on experience in a major banking environment.

The position was posted on August 18, 2026, and is listed as available in five locations across the Truist footprint. The supplied job announcement does not specify a closing date, meaning interested candidates should not wait for a deadline before submitting an application.

About the Truist 2027 Credit Internship Program

The Credit Internship Program is a temporary internship opportunity designed to develop early-career talent for roles connected to Truist’s Wholesale Banking business.

Rather than focusing exclusively on classroom learning, the programme combines structured training with practical assignments and exposure to real business activities.

Interns can expect to participate in:

  • Educational and professional development sessions.
  • Business rotations.
  • Special projects and assignments.
  • Day-to-day business activities.
  • Training related to credit and risk.
  • Team-based projects.
  • Activities involving internal business partners and external clients.
  • Exposure to senior leaders and, potentially, executive leaders.

This combination is intended to help interns understand how financial institutions operate while strengthening the technical, analytical, communication, and leadership capabilities required for a career in financial services.

What Is the Credit Track?

The Credit track is specifically aligned with business lines within Wholesale Banking.

Interns may gain exposure to areas such as:

Commercial and Corporate Banking

This area involves supporting businesses and corporate clients with financial services and banking solutions. Interns can gain insight into how financial institutions evaluate business needs, manage relationships, and assess financial and credit considerations.

Specialized Industries

This area focuses on specific industry sectors and their unique financial requirements. Exposure to specialized industries can help interns understand how economic conditions, industry dynamics, and business models influence financial decision-making.

Wholesale Payments

Wholesale Payments focuses on financial solutions and payment services for business and institutional clients. Exposure to this area can help interns understand the role of financial infrastructure and payment systems in supporting businesses.

The specific business area assigned to an intern will depend on the host team and programme placement.

What Can Interns Expect During the Program?

Truist describes the programme as one that combines education, exposure, and experience.

This means successful interns are not simply expected to observe employees. They will have opportunities to participate in work that supports internal business partners and external clients while applying concepts learned during training.

Interns will also be expected to work collaboratively and contribute to projects and activities assigned by their rotational leads.

The programme is therefore suitable for students who want to gain practical experience while developing a deeper understanding of financial services.

Exposure to Truist Senior Leaders

One notable feature of the programme is exposure to Truist senior leadership.

The internship may include sessions involving senior leaders and executive leaders, giving participants an opportunity to learn about the organization, its business operations, and the expectations associated with careers in financial services.

For students preparing for careers in banking, finance, credit, or related areas, this type of professional exposure can provide useful insight into the financial-services industry and corporate leadership.

Key Responsibilities of a Credit Intern

Successful interns will be expected to undertake a range of responsibilities throughout the programme.

1. Learn Credit and Risk Management Concepts

Interns will learn a broad range of concepts related to risk management, enterprise programmes and financial services.

This training is intended to prepare them for assignments within different lines of business.

2. Develop Analytical and Decision-Making Skills

Credit and financial-services careers require employees to evaluate information, identify risks, and make informed decisions.

The programme therefore emphasizes the development of analytical and decision-making capabilities.

Interns will have opportunities to apply these skills through practical projects and business assignments.

3. Strengthen Communication Skills

Effective communication is an important requirement of the internship.

Interns may work with internal business partners, external clients, managers, and other members of their teams. They will therefore need to communicate information clearly and professionally.

4. Develop Leadership Skills

The programme also seeks to strengthen leadership capabilities.

Students can develop leadership skills through project participation, teamwork, initiative, campus involvement, and other professional responsibilities.

5. Complete Special Projects

Interns may be assigned special projects or other tasks outside the formal training programme.

These assignments can provide opportunities to demonstrate initiative, analytical thinking, organization and problem-solving skills.

6. Participate in Business Rotations

Business rotations form an important part of the programme.

Through rotations, interns can work on projects and participate in normal business activities, allowing them to apply concepts and behaviours learned during training.

7. Complete Additional Training

Managers may recommend additional training during or after the internship programme.

This can help interns continue developing relevant skills and knowledge based on their assignments and career interests.

Academic Requirements

The Truist Credit Internship Program is intended for students who are actively pursuing a university degree.

Applicants must be working toward either:

  • A Bachelor’s degree; or
  • A Master’s degree.

Truist particularly values candidates studying business-related disciplines, with accounting and finance coursework preferred.

A 3.0 or higher GPA is preferred.

The GPA requirement is described as preferred rather than an absolute minimum, meaning candidates should carefully review the complete application requirements rather than assuming that applicants below 3.0 are automatically excluded.

Graduation Requirement

Another important requirement concerns the expected graduation date.

Applicants should have a scheduled final-degree graduation date between the following:

December 2027 and June 2029.

Students outside this graduation window may therefore not fit the target profile for this particular internship programme.

Prospective applicants should carefully compare their expected graduation date with the requirement before applying.

Skills Truist Is Looking For

The programme is designed for students who can demonstrate a combination of academic preparation, interpersonal abilities, and professional potential.

Important skills and qualities include:

Strong Communication

Candidates should possess excellent interpersonal and communication skills.

This is important because interns may work with multiple stakeholders, participate in meetings, collaborate on projects, and potentially interact with clients.

Initiative

Truist seeks students who demonstrate strong initiative.

Applicants should be able to show situations where they have taken responsibility, identified opportunities, solved problems, or gone beyond basic expectations.

Leadership

Demonstrated leadership is another important requirement.

Leadership may be demonstrated through:

  • Campus organizations.
  • Student leadership positions.
  • Volunteer activities.
  • Work experience.
  • Academic projects.
  • Community initiatives.
  • Team activities.
  • Other situations where the applicant has taken responsibility and influenced positive outcomes.

Analytical Ability

Because the Credit track is associated with credit and risk, analytical thinking is highly relevant.

Students should be comfortable working with information, evaluating situations, and drawing logical conclusions.

Financial Services Interest

Candidates should have genuine enthusiasm for pursuing a career in financial services.

A demonstrated interest in banking, finance, credit, accounting, risk management, or related fields can strengthen an applicant’s profile.

Technical Skills Required

Applicants should be proficient in:

  • Microsoft Excel
  • Microsoft PowerPoint

Excel is particularly useful in financial-services environments where employees may work with financial information, calculations, analysis, and reporting.

PowerPoint can be useful for presentations, project updates, business proposals, and communicating analytical findings.

Students should therefore ensure that they can confidently use both programmes before entering the internship.

Financial Services Knowledge

Truist also seeks candidates with general knowledge of the financial services industry.

Students should therefore understand fundamental concepts related to banking, finance, credit, and risk.

Applicants do not necessarily need extensive professional experience because the programme is designed for early-career talent. However, demonstrating an informed interest in financial services can help distinguish a candidate.

Relocation Requirement

The internship is not necessarily conducted in one fixed location.

Truist states that individuals hired into the programme will relocate throughout the Truist footprint based on their assigned host team.

The specific location will be included in the internship offer letter.

Applicants should therefore be prepared to relocate if required.

This is an important consideration for students who currently live outside the assigned internship location.

Travel Requirement

Candidates must also demonstrate a willingness to travel for on-the-job training.

Students considering this opportunity should therefore be comfortable with travel and potential changes in work location associated with training and programme activities.

Hybrid Learning and Training

Training sessions throughout the summer may use a hybrid approach, combining remote and in-person learning.

This provides flexibility while still allowing interns to participate in face-to-face professional development and workplace experiences.

The precise balance between remote and in-person activities may depend on the programme and assigned team.

Employment Authorization Requirement

One of the most important eligibility considerations is Truist’s employment-authorization policy.

The company explicitly states that it will not sponsor applicants for employment authorization for this position.

The company also states that it will not provide immigration-related support for several categories of immigration status, including:

  • H-1B;
  • F-1 OPT;
  • F-1 STEM OPT;
  • F-1 CPT;
  • J-1;
  • TN-1;
  • TN-2;
  • E-3; and
  • Sponsorship for U.S. permanent residence.

Applicants should therefore carefully assess their existing U.S. employment authorization before applying.

This requirement is particularly important for international students studying in the United States who may normally rely on post-study or student-related employment authorization.

English Language Requirement

The job posting identifies English as required.

Candidates should therefore have sufficient English-language proficiency to communicate effectively in a professional banking environment.

This includes the ability to participate in meetings, communicate with colleagues, prepare professional documents and presentations, and interact appropriately with internal and external stakeholders.

Internship Employment Type

The position is classified as temporary.

This is consistent with its structure as an internship programme designed to provide students with professional experience before completion of their degree.

Students should therefore distinguish the programme from a permanent full-time position.

Internship Locations

The job posting states that the Credit Internship Program is available in five locations.

The specific location for an individual intern will depend on the assigned host team and will be communicated in the offer letter.

Because relocation is part of the programme expectations, applicants should be prepared to work at the location assigned to them.

Compensation Information

For work locations in Washington, D.C., the posting states an annualized hourly wage of:

$25.00 per hour.

The posting provides this figure specifically to comply with Washington, D.C. pay transparency requirements.

Applicants should note that the stated rate applies to Washington, D.C. work locations and should not automatically be assumed to apply to every location where the internship is available.

Benefits Information

The job posting includes a general description of benefits available to eligible Truist employees.

However, it specifically explains that regular employees working 20 hours or more per week may be eligible for benefits, while temporary or contingent workers may not qualify for the same benefits.

The posting therefore advises applicants to review the specific benefits applicable to their employment status and position.

General Truist benefits described in the posting include the following:

  • Medical coverage.
  • Dental coverage.
  • Vision coverage.
  • Life insurance.
  • Disability coverage.
  • Accidental death and dismemberment coverage.
  • Tax-preferred savings accounts.
  • 401(k) plan.
  • Vacation.
  • Sick days.
  • Paid holidays.

Eligibility for specific benefits depends on employment classification, division, hours worked, and other applicable conditions.

Truist’s Purpose and Values

Truist states that its purpose is to inspire and build better lives and communities.

The company emphasizes caring for clients, empowering teammates, and serving communities.

The organization provides services across areas including:

  • Consumer banking.
  • Wholesale banking.
  • Technology.
  • Data.
  • Operations.

Interns are expected to embrace and model Truist’s purpose, mission, and values during the programme.

Equal Employment Opportunity

Truist states that it is an Equal Opportunity Employer.

The company says it does not discriminate based on characteristics including:

  • Race.
  • Gender.
  • Color.
  • Religion.
  • Citizenship.
  • National origin.
  • Age.
  • Sexual orientation.
  • Gender identity.
  • Disability.
  • Veteran status.
  • Other classifications protected by law.

The opportunity, therefore, does not specify a particular race, ethnicity, or continent as a prerequisite.

However, the employment-authorization requirement remains an important condition for applicants.

Who Should Apply?

The opportunity is particularly suitable for students who are:

  • Studying finance, accounting, business, or a related field.
  • Pursuing a Bachelor’s or Master’s degree.
  • Expected to graduate between December 2027 and June 2029.
  • Interested in banking and financial services.
  • Interested in credit and risk management.
  • Comfortable working with Excel and PowerPoint.
  • Strong communicators.
  • Analytical and detail-oriented.
  • Demonstrated leaders.
  • Proactive and willing to take initiative.
  • Comfortable working collaboratively.
  • Willing to travel.
  • Willing to relocate.
  • Authorized to work in the United States without requiring sponsorship.

How Applicants Can Prepare a Strong Application

Students interested in the Truist Credit Internship Program should approach the application strategically.

1. Review Your Graduation Date

Confirm that your expected final-degree graduation date falls between December 2027 and June 2029.

2. Highlight Relevant Coursework

If you are studying business, accounting, finance, or another related field, make sure relevant coursework is clearly reflected in your application.

Courses related to financial analysis, accounting, economics, corporate finance, banking, risk management, or related areas can demonstrate alignment with the Credit track.

3. Demonstrate Leadership

Do not simply state that you have leadership skills.

Provide examples of how you have demonstrated leadership through campus organizations, employment, academic projects, community initiatives, or other activities.

4. Emphasize Analytical Skills

Highlight academic, professional, or extracurricular experiences that required research, analysis, problem-solving, or decision-making.

5. Demonstrate Financial Services Interest

Explain why you are interested in banking, credit, risk, or financial services and how the internship fits into your longer-term career objectives.

6. Strengthen Your Excel and PowerPoint Skills

Because Excel and PowerPoint proficiency is specifically listed among the requirements, applicants should ensure that these skills are clearly represented in their resumes and applications where appropriate.

7. Prepare for Relocation

Applicants should be comfortable with the possibility of relocating within the Truist footprint.

8. Confirm Employment Authorization

This is particularly important for international students and other candidates who may require immigration support.

Truist explicitly states that it will not sponsor employment authorization for this internship, so applicants should confirm that they independently meet the employment-authorization requirement before applying.

Key Facts About the Truist 2027 Credit Internship Program

Feature Details
Opportunity 2027 Credit Internship Program
Organization Truist
Category Internship
Employment type Temporary
Sector Banking and financial services
Track Credit
Business area Wholesale Banking
Degree level Bachelor’s or Master’s
Preferred fields Business, accounting and finance
Preferred GPA 3.0+
Graduation window December 2027 to June 2029
Language English required
Technical skills Excel and PowerPoint
Locations Five U.S. locations
Relocation Required based on assigned host team
Travel Required for on-the-job training
U.S. work authorization Required; no sponsorship
Washington, D.C. stated wage $25 per hour
Posted August 18, 2026
Application deadline Not specified in the provided posting

Is There an Application Deadline?

The supplied Truist job announcement does not provide a specific application closing date.

Because internship recruitment can be competitive and positions can close when hiring needs are met, students who meet the requirements should consider applying as soon as possible rather than waiting for a deadline to be announced.

The posting was published on August 18, 2026.

Application Process

Candidates interested in the Truist 2027 Credit Internship Program should use the official Truist careers platform to review the position and submit an application.

The job posting explains that applicants should click the Apply Now button and complete the application.

After completing the application, candidates will be invited to create a profile that allows them to:

  • Track their application status.
  • Receive communications relating to their application.
  • Access relevant recruitment information.

Candidates who already have a Truist profile can log in to review their application status.

APPLY HERE

Application Accommodation

Truist states that candidates with disabilities who require assistance during the application process may request a reasonable accommodation.

The recruitment information provides a dedicated accessibility contact for accommodation requests.

Applicants requiring an accommodation should use the official contact information provided in the Truist job announcement rather than sending unrelated recruitment inquiries through the accommodation channel.

Why This Internship Could Be Valuable for Students

The Credit Internship Program is structured around three central components: education, exposure, and experience.

Students receive structured learning while gaining exposure to professionals and senior leaders and participating in practical business activities.

The Credit track can be particularly relevant for students considering careers in:

  • Commercial banking.
  • Corporate banking.
  • Credit analysis.
  • Risk management.
  • Wholesale banking.
  • Financial services.
  • Financial analysis.
  • Banking operations.
  • Specialized industry banking.
  • Wholesale payments.

The experience can help students understand how financial concepts are applied in a professional environment while developing transferable skills in communication, analysis, leadership, and teamwork.

Visit HERE for more information about the Truist 2027 Credit Internship Program.

Conclusion

The Truist 2027 Credit Internship Program is a strong early-career opportunity for students pursuing degrees in business, finance, accounting, and related disciplines who want to gain practical experience in the financial services industry.

The programme combines structured education with professional exposure, business rotations, special projects, and practical assignments. Interns can develop their understanding of credit, risk management, and wholesale banking while strengthening analytical, communication, and leadership skills.

The programme is particularly suited to students graduating between December 2027 and June 2029, with a preferred GPA of 3.0 or higher and an interest in financial services. Applicants should also be proficient in Excel and PowerPoint, demonstrate leadership and initiative, and be willing to travel and relocate according to their assigned host team.

A critical consideration for applicants is U.S. employment authorization. Truist explicitly states that it will not provide employment sponsorship or immigration-related support for this position. Candidates should therefore verify their eligibility to work in the United States before submitting an application.

The posting was published on August 18, 2026, and no specific application deadline is stated in the provided announcement. Given the competitive nature of internship recruitment, eligible students should review the official posting and submit their applications as early as possible.

For students seeking to turn their academic knowledge into practical experience in credit, banking, and financial services, the Truist 2027 Credit Internship Program provides an opportunity to learn, contribute, and build a foundation for a future career in the financial sector.

For more global Internship opportunities, visit OFY HERE.
